Es bietet ein interdisziplinäres Umfeld für die Forschung an der Schnittstelle von Humanbiologie, Technologie und klinische Übersetzung. Projekt Hintergrund Schlaf, Stress und Arousal sind zutiefst vernetzte physiologische Prozesse. Dauerhafter Stress und erhöhte Arousal können den Übergang in den Schlaf ändern, nächtliches Gehirn und autonome Aktivität ändern, und Einfluss auf Erholung, Widerstandsfähigkeit und längerfristige Gesundheit. Dennoch werden noch viele Schlüsselmechanismen entweder in streng kontrollierten Laboreinstellungen oder durch vereinfachte reale Maßnahmen untersucht, die den Reichtum der menschlichen Physiologie nicht erfassen. Dieses Projekt behandelt diese Lücke durch die Kombination von mechanistischen In-Lab-Studien mit der realen Welt-Phänotypisierung von Schlaf, Stress und Arousal im täglichen Leben. Ziel ist es, strenge, skalierbare Forschungs-Workflows zu entwickeln, die messen können, wie Stress und Arousal sich über den Tag entfalten, wie sie die Schlaf- und Übernachtungserholung beeinflussen und welche physiologischen Signaturen am informativsten für gesundheitsrelevante Phänotypen sind. Das Projekt wird multimodale Biosignalerfassung, wie Pupillometrie, Schlaf EEG, ECG, Atmungs-, Wearable- und Aktigraphiedaten, Smartphone-gestützte Bewertungen und validierte Fragebogen zusammen mit fortschrittlicher Signalverarbeitung, statistischer Modellierung und maschinellem Lernen verwenden. Der Doktorand wird dabei helfen, Studien zu implementieren, zu koordinieren und zu analysieren, die kontrollierte Physiologie und ökologische, hausbasierte Beurteilung überbrücken. Jobbeschreibung Der erfolgreiche Kandidat entwickelt, führt und analysiert menschliche Studien, die Schlaf, Stress, arousale und autonome Physiologie in Labor- und Real-Welt-Einstellungen verbinden. Ein zentraler Teil der Position wird die Implementierung robuster Forschungspipelines für mobile und dezentrale Phänotypisierung sein, einschließlich Datenerfassungs-Workflows, Biosignalverarbeitung, Qualitätskontrolle, Synchronisation, Merkmalsextraktion und Rechenanalyse. Die Position ist ideal für einen Kandidat, der auf menschliche Physiologie, Schlafforschung, mobile Gesundheitsmethoden und eine starke Rechendatenanalyse kombinieren will. Professionelle Software-Ingenieure können Teile des technischen Rückgrats unterstützen, aber der Doktorand sollte in der Lage sein, den Datenfluss zu implementieren und zu verstehen, mit technischen Mitarbeitern zu arbeiten, forschungsorientierte Pipelines zu implementieren und wissenschaftliches Eigentum an den physiologischen Daten und seiner Interpretation zu nehmen. Mansion - Entwurf und Durchführung mechanistischer Laborstudien und realer Schlaf, Stress und Arousalstudien an menschlichen Teilnehmern - Erkundigen und verwalten Sie multimodale physiologische Daten während Wake und Sleep wie Pupillometrie, EEG, ECG, Atmung, Photoplethysmographie, Aktigraphie, tragbare Sensordaten, Smartphone-basierte Bewertungen und Fragebogen - C
descriptionByLocale.fr: Descrizione Position du doctorat sur le sommeil, le stress et l'excitation chez les humains 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Un environnement de recherche de calibre mondial à l'intersection des technologies du sommeil, de la physiologie et de la santé Le Neural Control of Movement Lab de l'ETH Zurich, Département des sciences et technologies de la santé, invite des candidats exceptionnels à postuler à un poste de doctorat axé sur les liens physiologiques entre le sommeil, le stress, l'excitation et la santé chez l'homme. Le projet combine des expériences de laboratoire mécanistes avec le phénotypage réel, à domicile et décentralisé, en utilisant des enregistrements physiologiques multimodaux, des technologies de santé mobiles et des pipelines d'analyse computationnelle. Le Neural Control of Movement Lab se concentre sur la compréhension de la façon dont le cerveau contrôle le comportement et sur le développement d'interfaces non invasives pour mesurer et moduler la fonction cérébrale pendant le réveil et le sommeil. Dans ce contexte, le doctorant contribuera à un programme de recherche translationnelle qui vise à comprendre comment le stress quotidien et les états d'excitation façonnent la physiologie du sommeil, le rétablissement et les résultats pertinents pour la santé dans la vie réelle. Le Département des sciences de la santé et de la technologie de l'ETH Zurich réunit des chercheurs dans les domaines des neurosciences, de l'ingénierie biomédicale, des sciences du mouvement, de la nutrition, de la physiologie et de la médecine. Il offre un environnement interdisciplinaire pour la recherche à l'interface de la biologie humaine, de la technologie et de la traduction clinique. Contexte du projet Le sommeil, le stress et l'excitation sont des processus physiologiques profondément interconnectés. Le stress persistant et l'excitation accrue peuvent modifier la transition vers le sommeil, changer le cerveau nocturne et l'activité autonome, et influencer la récupération, la résilience et la santé à long terme. Pourtant, de nombreux mécanismes clés sont encore étudiés soit dans des laboratoires étroitement contrôlés, soit par des mesures simplifiées du monde réel qui ne saisissent pas la richesse de la physiologie humaine. Ce projet vise à combler cette lacune en combinant des études mécanistes en laboratoire avec le phénotypage réel du sommeil, du stress et de l'excitation dans la vie quotidienne. L'objectif est d'élaborer des flux de travail de recherche rigoureux et évolutifs qui permettent de mesurer comment le stress et l'excitation se déroulent au cours de la journée, comment ils affectent le sommeil et la récupération du jour au lendemain, et quelles signatures physiologiques sont les plus informatives pour les phénotypes pertinents pour la santé. Le projet utilisera l'acquisition de biosignaux multimodaux, tels que la pupillométrie, l'EEG du sommeil, l'ECG, la respiration, les données portables et actigraphiques, les évaluations soutenues par smartphone et les questionnaires validés, ainsi que le traitement avancé des signaux, la modélisation statistique et l'apprentissage automatique. Le doctorant aidera à mettre en oeuvre, coordonner et analyser les études qui relient la physiologie contrôlée et l'évaluation écologique à domicile. Description du poste Le candidat retenu concevra, mènera et analysera des études humaines sur le sommeil, le stress, l'excitation et la physiologie autonome en laboratoire et dans le monde réel. Un élément central de la position sera la mise en place de pipelines de recherche robustes pour le phénotypage mobile et décentralisé, y compris les flux de travail de collecte de données, le traitement des biosignales, le contrôle de la qualité, la synchronisation, l'extraction de fonctionnalités et l'analyse computationnelle. Le poste est idéal pour un candidat qui veut combiner la physiologie humaine pratique, la recherche sur le sommeil, les méthodes de santé mobiles et une analyse de données computationnelles solide. Les ingénieurs en logiciels professionnels peuvent soutenir des parties de l'épine dorsale technique, mais le doctorant devrait être en mesure de mettre en œuvre et de comprendre le flux de données, de travailler avec des collaborateurs techniques, de mettre en place des pipelines faisant face à la recherche et de s'approprier scientifiquement les données physiologiques et leur interprétation. Mansioni - Concevoir et mener des études de laboratoire mécanistes et des études sur le sommeil, le stress et l'excitation dans le monde réel chez les participants humains - Acquérir et gérer des données physiologiques multimodales pendant le sillage et le sommeil telles que pupillométrie, EEG, ECG, respiration, photopléthysmographie, actigraphie, données de capteur portable, évaluations basées sur smartphone et questionnaires - C

jobs.description:
DevOps Engineer

80%-100%, Lugano, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) develops and operates a high-performance computing and data research infrastructure that supports world-class science in Switzerland. Its user laboratory is available to domestic and international researchers in academia, industry, and the business sector. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices at its data centre in Lugano and in Zurich.

For this position the preferred work location is Lugano, but it could also be Zürich.

Project background

We are seeking a versatile and driven DevOps Engineer to help design, build, and operate the software-defined infrastructure and services powering advanced scientific computing and AI/ML workloads at scale.

You will work at the intersection of systems engineering, software engineering, cloud-native infrastructure, and high-performance computing (HPC), contributing to platforms and services used by researchers and engineers tackling complex scientific and AI challenges.

We value strong engineering fundamentals, curiosity, adaptability, and willingness to learn more than a perfect initial match of technical requirements. We welcome engineers from diverse backgrounds who are eager to contribute and grow. If you are motivated by challenging technical environments and enjoy understanding systems deeply, we strongly encourage you to apply even if your experience does not cover every area listed below.

We are offering a contract initially limited to two years , which will provide the opportunity to contribute to a fast-evolving AI landscape in which CSCS plays a key role and to support high-impact initiatives both nationally and internationally. This includes contributions to the Swiss AI Initiative and similar programs, such as lending support for the development and release of the Apertus models.

The initial two-year contract could potentially be extended or even become permanent.

Job description

• Design, deploy, automate, and operate scalable infrastructure and cloud-native platform services

• Contribute to Kubernetes-based AI/ML and HPC platforms, including CI/CD, GitOps, observability, security, and operational tooling

• Collaborate with researchers and engineers to support complex workflows, troubleshoot production environments, and improve reliability and performance

• Contribute to platform engineering, automation, and developer productivity initiatives across evolving systems and services

• The technologies and areas below illustrate the breadth of our environment and interests. They are not a checklist of requirements, and experience in only some of these areas is expected

Profile

Technical environment and areas of interest:

• Linux systems engineering, and software development (e.g., Python, Bash)

• Containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD, GitOps, and Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform, Helm, Ansible, ArgoCD)

• Distributed systems concepts, APIs, scalability, observability, identity and access management, and security

• AI/ML platforms and supporting infrastructure services

• HPC systems, GPU clusters, and large-scale infrastructure environments

• Platform engineering and developer productivity tooling

• Secure or confidentiality-sensitive operational environments

Personal qualities:

• Curious, hands-on, and eager to understand systems inside-out

• Strong engineering mindset and problem-solving attitude

• Comfortable learning new technologies and working across disciplines

• Effective communicator and collaborative team player

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• Experience supporting research or scientific computing environments

• Familiarity with HPC systems and services

• Exposure to GPU clusters and accelerated computing

• Experience with SRE p

Questo include i contributi all'Iniziativa dell'AI svizzera e programmi simili, come il supporto di prestito per lo sviluppo e il rilascio dei modelli Apertus. Il contratto iniziale di due anni potrebbe potenzialmente essere esteso o addirittura diventare permanente. Descrizione del lavoro
• Progettazione, distribuzione, automatizzazione e gestione di infrastrutture scalabili e servizi piattaforma cloud-native
• Contribuire a piattaforme AI/ML e HPC basate su Kubernetes, tra cui CI/CD, GitOps, osservabilità, sicurezza e strumenti operativi
• Collaborare con ricercatori e ingegneri per supportare flussi di lavoro complessi, risolvere gli ambienti di produzione e migliorare affidabilità e prestazioni
• Contribuire alle iniziative di ingegneria, automazione e produttività degli sviluppatori in sistemi e servizi in evoluzione
• Le tecnologie e le aree sottostanti illustrano la vastità del nostro ambiente e degli interessi. Non sono una lista di controllo dei requisiti, e l'esperienza in solo alcune di queste aree è previsto Profilo Ambiente tecnico e aree di interesse:
• Ingegneria dei sistemi Linux, scripting, risoluzione dei problemi e sviluppo del software (ad esempio, Python, Bash)
• Contenitori, Kubernetes, CI/CD, GitOps e Infrastrutture come Codice (ad esempio, Terraform, Helm, Ansible, ArgoCD)
• Concetti di sistemi distribuiti, API, scalabilità, osservabilità, gestione dell'identità e dell'accesso, e sicurezza
• piattaforme AI/ML e servizi di infrastruttura di supporto
• Sistemi HPC, cluster GPU e ambienti infrastrutturali su larga scala
• Strumento di ingegneria della piattaforma e produttività dello sviluppatore
• Ambienti operativi sicuri o sensibili alla riservatezza Qualità personali:
• Curioso, pratico e desideroso di capire i sistemi all'interno
• Forte mentalità ingegneristica e atteggiamento problem solving
• Confortevole apprendimento di nuove tecnologie e di lavoro attraverso le discipline
• Efficace comunicatore e collaboratore Modi per distinguersi dalla folla:
• Esperienza di supporto alla ricerca o agli ambienti di calcolo scientifico
• Familiarità con sistemi e servizi HPC
• Esposizione a cluster GPU e calcolo accelerato

Das Anwenderlabor ist für inländische und internationale Forscher in Wissenschaft, Industrie und Wirtschaft verfügbar. Für diese Position ist der bevorzugte Arbeitsort Lugano, aber es könnte auch Zürich sein. Projekt Hintergrund Wir suchen einen vielseitigen und angetriebenen DevOps Engineer, um die softwaredefinierte Infrastruktur und Dienstleistungen zu entwerfen, zu bauen und zu betreiben, die fortschrittliche wissenschaftliche Computing- und AI/ML-Workloads im Maßstab vorantreiben. Wir schätzen starke Engineering-Grundsätze, Neugier, Anpassungsfähigkeit und Bereitschaft, mehr als eine perfekte Erstanpassung an technische Anforderungen zu lernen. Wir begrüßen Ingenieure aus unterschiedlichen Hintergründen, die gerne dazu beitragen und wachsen. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices at its data centre in Lugano and in Zurich.

For this position the work location is Lugano.

Project background

As high-performance computing, AI, and cloud technologies continue to converge; CSCS is redefining how advanced computational services are designed and delivered. Modern scientific and engineering workloads are no longer just large—they are complex, data-intensive, and highly diverse, pushing existing infrastructure to its limits.

We are offering a contract initially limited to two years , which will provide the opportunity to contribute to a fast-evolving AI landscape in which CSCS plays a key role and to support high-impact initiatives both nationally and internationally. This includes contributions to the Swiss AI Initiative and similar programs, such as lending support for the development and release of foundation models in the weather and climate domain.

The initial two-year contract could potentially be extended or even become permanent.

Job description

The main goal of this position is to develop and manage HPC/AI services on top of a multi-tenant infrastructure. As a Platform automation engineer, you will directly contribute to the design, implementation, maintenance, and documentation of platform services to support HPC and AI. Your work will directly enhance the overall system functionality and efficiency.

Main duties:

• Investigating, troubleshooting, and debugging platform services and infrastructure resources

• Developing, maintaining, and supporting tools and pipelines to support platforms on a geographically redundant infrastructure

• Developing automations to provision, test, deploy, and monitor resources to support the needs of HPC and AI platforms

• Supporting, documenting, and sharing knowledge of tools, and procedur

Profile

You should have a bachelor’s or higher degree in computer engineering, computer science, a relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

You should have a sound knowledge of:

• Experience in the deployment of HPC, AI, or Cloud infrastructures

• Management of HPC/AI services to maximize utilization of compute, storage and high speed network components

• Working knowledge of automation tools and frameworks, including CI/CD processes and ecosystem

• Linux administration skills

Experience with the following is preferred, though there will be ample opportunities to learn and gain more experience with all of these skills on the job:

• Versioning systems and CI/CD workflows such as ArgoCD

• Debugging of microservices running on Kubernetes

• Performance monitoring and diagnostic tools for HPC/AI hardware

jobs.description:
PhD Position in Numerical Modelling of Debris Flows

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Engineering Geology (Prof. Dr. Jordan Aaron, Geological Institute) is looking for a creative and motivated PhD candidate with a strong interest in fluid mechanics and numerical modelling. The position is expected to start in September 2026 and is fully funded for 4 years.

Job description

• You will develop a new coupled solid/ fluid mechanics-based numerical model to simulate the motion of debris flows

• You will incorporate novel field data currently being collected at numerous locations around the world to validate the new numerical model

• You will combine the numerical model results with field data to further our understanding of the motion of debris flows

Profile

• MSc in Fluid Mechanics, Hydraulics, Engineering Geology, Geological Engineering, Geophysics or related fields

• Strong background in numerical modelling

• Interest in natural hazards

• Motivation, creativity, independence, and ability to work in a team

• Excellent English communication skills

Workplace

We offer

We are an enthusiastic and collaborative research group with many opportunities for multi-disciplinary cutting-edge research in engineering geology. There are significant opportunities to broaden your research interests and develop your academic career. We further offer training in teaching through teaching assistantships, as well as access to state-of-the-art computing infrastructure, laboratories, and research equipment.

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application until 1 July 2026 with the following documents:

• A brief cover letter summarizing your motivation to apply for the position.

• Your CV

• Transcripts

• The contact details of two references

Further information about the Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences can be found on our website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Prof. Jordan Aaron, jordan.aaron@eaps.ethz.ch (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

About ETH Zürich

ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

jobs.description:
PhD Position in Computer Vision Applied to Natural Hazards

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Engineering Geology group at ETH Zurich (Prof. Jordan Aaron) is seeking a motivated and creative doctoral student who specializes in computer vision. The position can commence as early as September 1st, 2026 (negotiable), and is fully funded for four years.

Job description

• Improving our understanding of the mechanisms that govern debris flow motion is a core research topic in the Chair of Engineering Geology at ETHZ

• As part of this, the group collects and analyses an unprecendented set of field datasets

• The collected data includes timelapse point clouds, video imagery, as well as auxilary data including environmental parameter timeseries

• This data is then processed to derive high temporal and spatial resolution estimates of displacement, velocity, strain and surface change, as well as the driving mechanisms

• A large foundational dataset has already been collected, and presents a unique opportunity for making new insights into debris-flow processes

• You will develop advanced algorithms to process this data, with a focus on optical flow and object detection

• You will interpret the results to better understand debris flow mechanisms

• You will also contribute to the maintenance and upkeep of the monitoring systems

• Additionally, you will be given signficiant support to develop your own research ideas and apply for third party funding

• Contributions to teaching within the Engineering Geology group are also expected

Profile

• Masters degree in Computer Vision, Data Science, Computer Science, Mechatronics, Remote Sensing, Engineering Geology or other related discipline

• Demonstrated expertise and interest in machine learning and computer vision algorithms is necessary, with an emphasis on object tracking, optical flow and sensor fusion

• Knowledge of rock mechanics, soil mechanics and/or landslide processes is considered beneficial

• Prior experience with point cloud processing is an asset

• Ability to work independently

• Strong written and oral communication skills in English

Workplace

We offer

• We are an enthusiastic and collaborative research group with many opportunities for multi-disciplinary cutting edge research in engineering geology

• There are significant opportunities to broaden your research interests, and develop your academic career

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Poste de doctorat en vision informatique appliquée aux risques naturels 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le groupe de géologie d'ingénierie de l'ETH Zurich (prof. Jordan Aaron) cherche un doctorant motivé et créatif qui se spécialise dans la vision informatique. Le poste peut commencer dès le 1er septembre 2026 (négociable) et est entièrement financé pendant quatre ans. Description du poste
• Améliorer notre compréhension des mécanismes qui régissent le mouvement de l'écoulement des débris est un thème de recherche essentiel de la chaire d'ingénierie géologique à ETHZ
• Dans ce cadre, le groupe recueille et analyse un ensemble de données de terrain non précendentes
• Les données collectées comprennent les nuages ponctuels, les images vidéo, ainsi que les données auxiliaires, y compris les séries chronologiques des paramètres environnementaux
• Ces données sont ensuite traitées pour obtenir des estimations de haute résolution temporelle et spatiale du déplacement, de la vitesse, de la déformation et du changement de surface, ainsi que des mécanismes de conduite
• Un vaste ensemble de données fondamentales a déjà été collecté et offre une occasion unique de faire de nouveaux éclairages sur les processus d'écoulement des débris.
• Vous développerez des algorithmes avancés pour traiter ces données, en mettant l'accent sur le flux optique et la détection d'objets
• Vous interpréterez les résultats pour mieux comprendre les mécanismes d'écoulement des débris
• Vous contribuerez également à l'entretien et à l'entretien des systèmes de surveillance
• En outre, vous bénéficierez d'un soutien significatif pour développer vos propres idées de recherche et faire une demande de financement par des tiers
• Des contributions à l'enseignement au sein du groupe d'ingénierie géologique sont également attendues Profil
• Maîtrise en informatique, informatique, mécatronique, télédétection, géologie ou autre discipline connexe
• Une expertise démontrée et un intérêt pour l'apprentissage automatique et les algorithmes de vision par ordinateur sont nécessaires, en mettant l'accent sur le suivi des objets, le flux optique et la fusion des capteurs
• La connaissance de la mécanique des roches, de la mécanique des sols et/ou des processus de glissement de terrain est considérée comme bénéfique
• L'expérience préalable avec le traitement point cloud est un atout
• Capacité de travailler de manière indépendante
• Fortes compétences en communication écrite et orale en anglais Lieu de travail Nous offrons
• Nous sommes un groupe de recherche enthousiaste et collaboratif qui offre de nombreuses possibilités de recherche multidisciplinaire de pointe en géologie de l'ingénierie

Doktorand:in in Rechtswissenschaften (m/w/d)

100%, Zürich, befristet

print
Drucken

Im Rahmen des SNF-geförderten Projekts „Responsible AI for the Swiss Judiciary" untersuchen wir gemeinsam mit Schweizer Gerichten, wie künstliche Intelligenz verantwortungsvoll in die Justiz integriert werden kann.

Projekthintergrund

Die Doktorandenstelle ist auf die empirische Erforschung von KI-gestützten Entscheidungshilfen in der Justiz ausgerichtet. Die doktorierende Person wird die Auswirkungen solcher Systeme auf die richterliche Praxis untersuchen – durch die Konzeption und Durchführung von Feldexperimenten in Zusammenarbeit mit Schweizer Gerichten sowie deren rechtliche und institutionelle Evaluation.

Stellenbeschreibung

• Untersuchung richterlicher Entscheidungsprozesse und juristischer Argumentation im Zusammenspiel mit KI-Tools

• Mitwirkung bei der Entwicklung von Experimentdesigns und Evaluierungsrahmen für KI-gestützte Entscheidungsfindung

• Zusammenarbeit mit dem technischen Team zur Erforschung der Interaktion zwischen KI-Systemen und juristischen Nutzern

• Publikation von Forschungsergebnissen in führenden Fachzeitschriften und Präsentation auf internationalen Konferenzen

• Die Stelle ist als kumulative Dissertation an der Schnittstelle von Rechtswissenschaft, Informatik und empirischer Sozialwissenschaft konzipiert

• Unsere Büros befinden sich in der Zürcher Innenstadt

• Die Arbeitssprachen sind Deutsch und Englisch

Profil

• Einen hervorragenden Bachelor- und Masterabschluss in Rechtswissenschaften von einer deutschsprachigen Universität (Deutschland, Österreich oder Schweiz) mitbringen

• Ein ausgeprägtes Interesse an den Auswirkungen von KI auf Recht und Gesellschaft haben

• Interesse an Feldexperimenten und experimentellen Forschungsdesigns mitbringen

• Die Bereitschaft zeigen, quantitative und empirische Forschungsmethoden zu erlernen und anzuwenden

• Über sehr gute Englischkenntnisse verfügen; Deutsch- und Französischkenntnisse sind von Vorteil

Arbeitsort

Wir bieten

• Ihr Beruf mit Wirkung: Werden Sie Teil der ETH Zürich, die nicht nur Ihre berufliche Entwicklung unterstützt, sondern auch aktiv zu positiven Veränderungen in der Gesellschaft beiträgt

• Es erwarten Sie zahlreiche Vergünstigungen , wie z.B. ÖV-Abonnemente und Car Sharing, ein breites Sportangebot des ASVZ , Kinderbetreuung sowie attraktive Vorsorgeleistungen

Auf unserer Webseite zur Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt erfahren Sie, wie wir ein faires und offenes Umfeld sicherstellen, in dem sich alle entwickeln und entfalten können. Dottorando/a in Giurisprudenza 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato --- descrizione As part of the SNSF-funded project „Responsible AI for the Swiss Judiciary, we are working together with Swiss courts to investigate how artificial intelligence can be responsibly integrated into justice. Project background The PhD student body is responsible for the empirical research of AI-based decision-making aids in the judiciary. The doctoral student will investigate the effects of such systems on judicial practice – through the design and implementation of field experiments in cooperation with Swiss courts and their legal and institutional evaluation. --- Mansioni - Investigation of judicial decision-making processes and legal argumentation in interaction with AI tools - Participation in the development of experimental design and evaluation frameworks for AI-based decision-making - Cooperation with the technical team to investigate the interaction between AI systems and legal users - Publication of research results in leading journals and presentation at international conferences - The body is conceived as a cumulative dissertation at the interface of law, computer science and empirical social science - Our offices are located in Zurich city centre - The working languages are German and English.
• Requisiti - Bring an excellent Bachelor and Master's degree in Law from a German-speaking university (Germany, Austria or Switzerland) - A strong interest in the impact of AI on law and society - Bringing interest in field experiments and experimental research designs - The willingness to learn and apply quantitative and empirical research methods - have very good English skills; German and French skills are advantageous --- Luogo di lavoro

jobs.description:
PhD Position in Vehicle Sensor and Remote Sensing Analysis for Road Safety

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Infrastructure Management, led by Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey within the Institute of Construction and Infrastructure Management of the Department of Civil, Enviromental, and Geomatic Engineering, has an opening for a PhD student. This position focuses on leveraging vehicle sensors, remote sensing, and machine learning to support modern urban road safety analysis as a part of a larger EU project.

Project background

The new EU Horizon project advances safe active mobility uptake and research by introducing a human-centred, evidence-based approach that integrates actual and perceived safety for pedestrians, cyclists, and micromobility users. Moving beyond conventional crash-focused approaches, it captures near-misses, dynamic interactions, and embodied safety experiences that shape behaviour and mode choice. The project combines multi-source traffic, infrastructure, vehicle, and health data with immersive eXtended Reality (XR) experimentation and explainable Artificial Intelligence to analyse safety-critical situations that are rare, underreported, or ethically impossible to observe in real traffic. Explainable AI ensures transparency and interpretability, supporting trust, transferability, and policy relevance. The project translates these insights into harmonised assessment methodologies, predictive models, and validated indicators, enabling robust evaluation and comparison of regulatory, infrastructural, technological, and behavioural interventions across Safe System Approach stakeholders. Special focus is placed on interactions between users with differing masses and speeds, including e-bikes, e-cargo bikes, and e-scooters, for both personal mobility and urban logistics. Large-scale pilots in four European cities validate methods in real traffic, support cross-city learning, and ensure applicability under diverse safety, infrastructure and cultural conditions. Implemented by a multidisciplinary consortium bridging engineering, behavioural science, XR, AI, urban planning, and policy, the project delivers actionable, standardised guidance that accelerates safer, more inclusive active and micromobility systems across Europe.

Planning safe urban transport systems is inherently complex: interventions last for decades, require significant investment, must fit within constrained spaces, and must satisfy ever-changing user needs. Modern data collection methods - such as high-frequency on-board vehicle sensors and computer-vision imagery - are well-suited to capture these complexities via near real-time, high-resolution insights. However, collecting, processing, and operationalizing these big data volumes is a challenge due to heterogeneous data structures and heavy computational demands.

Job description

This doctorate aims to advance the state-of-the-art in sensor and remote sensing data fusion for urban transport infrastructure safety analysis. The candidate will develop new tools and methods that integrate big data, computer vision, and machine learning. The candidate’s core tasks will include:

• Develop a Scalable Sensing Pipeline: Design and implement a software/tool architecture capable of processing multi-source vehicle sensor, camera, and remote sensing data streams

• Automate Feature & Factor Identification: Train machine learning and computer vision models within the pipeline to automatically detect built-environment infrastructure characteristics and related factors affecting micromobility safety and comfort

• Generate Mapping & Diagnostic Outputs: Ensure the software accepts diverse inputs and generates structured, high-quality data outputs optimized for spatial mapping, risk diagnosis, and downstream predictive safety modelling

• Collaborate via Real-World Pilots: Validate and refine the pipeline using real-world data from the project’s pilot cities, working in close coope

descriptionByLocale.it:
Posizione del PhD nel sensore del veicolo e analisi di rilevamento remoto per la sicurezza stradale 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo La Cattedra di Gestione delle Infrastrutture, guidata dal Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey all'interno dell'Istituto di Costruzione e Gestione delle Infrastrutture del Dipartimento di Ingegneria Civile, Enviromentale e Geomatica, ha un'apertura per uno studente di dottorato. Questa posizione si concentra sulla leva dei sensori del veicolo, il telerilevamento e l'apprendimento automatico per supportare l'analisi moderna della sicurezza stradale urbana come parte di un progetto UE più ampio. Sfondo del progetto Il nuovo progetto EU Horizon promuove l'assorbimento e la ricerca di una mobilità attiva sicura introducendo un approccio basato su prove umane che integra la sicurezza reale e percepita per pedoni, ciclisti e utenti di micromobilità. Passando oltre i convenzionali approcci focalizzati agli urti, cattura vicino-misses, interazioni dinamiche e esperienze di sicurezza incarnate che modellano il comportamento e la scelta della modalità. Il progetto combina il traffico multi-fonte, l'infrastruttura, il veicolo e i dati sanitari con la sperimentazione immersiva eXtended Reality (XR) e l'intelligenza artificiale spiegabile per analizzare situazioni di sicurezza-critical che sono rare, sottovalutate, o eticamente impossibili da osservare nel traffico reale. La Spiegabile AI garantisce trasparenza e interpretabilità, sostenendo fiducia, trasferibilità e rilevanza politica. Il progetto traduce queste intuizioni in metodologie di valutazione armonizzate, modelli predittivi e indicatori convalidati, consentendo una valutazione e un confronto robusti di interventi normativi, infrastrutturali, tecnologici e comportamentali tra gli stakeholder di Safe System Approach. Particolare attenzione è posta sulle interazioni tra utenti con diverse masse e velocità, tra cui e-bike, e-cargo bike, e-scooters, sia per la mobilità personale che per la logistica urbana. I piloti su larga scala in quattro città europee convalidano i metodi nel traffico reale, supportano l'apprendimento trasversale e garantiscono l'applicabilità in diverse condizioni di sicurezza, infrastruttura e cultura. Implementato da un'ingegneria multidisciplinare di collegamento consortile, scienza comportamentale, XR, AI, pianificazione urbana e politica, il progetto offre una guida attuabile e standardizzata che accelera sistemi attivi e di micromobilità più sicuri e inclusivi in tutta Europa. La pianificazione di sistemi di trasporto urbano sicuri è intrinsecamente complessa: gli interventi durano per decenni, richiedono un investimento significativo, devono adattarsi all'interno di spazi limitati, e devono soddisfare le esigenze degli utenti in continua evoluzione. I moderni metodi di raccolta dei dati - come i sensori di veicoli a bordo ad alta frequenza e le immagini di computer-visione - sono adatti per catturare queste complessità attraverso intuizioni in tempo reale, ad alta risoluzione. Tuttavia, la raccolta, l'elaborazione e la operativizzazione di questi grandi volumi di dati è una sfida a causa di strutture di dati eterogenee e pesanti richieste computazionali. Descrizione del lavoro Questo dottorato mira a far progredire lo stato dell'arte nella fusione dei dati del sensore e del telerilevamento per l'analisi della sicurezza delle infrastrutture di trasporto urbano. Il candidato svilupperà nuovi strumenti e metodi che integrano grandi dati, visione del computer e machine learning. I compiti principali del candidato includono:
• Sviluppare una Pipeline di rilevamento scalabile: progettare e implementare un'architettura software/tool in grado di elaborare sensori, telecamere e flussi di dati di telerilevamento
• Identificazione automatica delle caratteristiche e dei fattori: Modelli di apprendimento della macchina da treno e visione del computer all'interno della pipeline per rilevare automaticamente le caratteristiche dell'infrastruttura dell'ambiente costruito e i fattori correlati che influenzano la sicurezza e il comfort della micromobilità
• Genera mappatura e uscite diagnostiche: Assicurarsi che il software accetti diversi input e genera uscite di dati strutturate e di alta qualità ottimizzate per mappatura spaziale, diagnosi di rischio e modellazione di sicurezza predittiva a valle
• Collaborare tramite Real-World Pilots: convalidare e perfezionare la pipeline utilizzando i dati reali delle città pilota del progetto, lavorando in stretta coope

PhD-Position im Fahrzeugsensor und Fernerkundungsanalyse für die Straßenverkehrssicherheit 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Der Lehrstuhl für Infrastrukturmanagement unter der Leitung von Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey im Institut für Bau- und Infrastrukturmanagement der Abteilung für Zivil-, Umwelt- und Geomatiktechnik hat eine Eröffnung für einen Doktoranden. Diese Position konzentriert sich auf die Verwendung von Fahrzeugsensoren, die Fernerkundung und das maschinelle Lernen, um die moderne städtische Verkehrssicherheitsanalyse im Rahmen eines größeren EU-Projekts zu unterstützen. Projekt Hintergrund Das neue EU-Horizont-Projekt fördert die sichere aktive Mobilitätsaufnahme und -forschung durch die Einführung eines menschenzentrierten, evidenzbasierten Ansatzes, der die tatsächliche und wahrgenommene Sicherheit für Fußgänger, Radfahrer und Mikromobilitätsnutzer integriert. Über konventionelle Crash-fokussierte Ansätze hinweg zu bewegen, erfasst sie Nah-Maßnahmen, dynamische Interaktionen und verkörperte Sicherheitserlebnisse, die Verhalten und Moduswahl prägen. Das Projekt kombiniert Mehrquellen-Verkehrs-, Infrastruktur-, Fahrzeug- und Gesundheitsdaten mit immersiven eXtended Reality (XR)-Experimenten und erklärbaren künstlichen Intelligenzen, um sicherheitskritische Situationen zu analysieren, die selten, unterreportiert oder ethisch unmöglich sind, im realen Verkehr zu beobachten. Erklärbare KI sorgt für Transparenz und Dolmetschbarkeit, Unterstützung von Vertrauen, Übertragbarkeit und politischer Relevanz. Das Projekt übersetzt diese Erkenntnisse zu harmonisierten Bewertungsmethoden, Prädiktionsmodellen und validierten Indikatoren, die eine robuste Bewertung und Vergleich von regulatorischen, infrastrukturellen, technologischen und verhaltensbezogenen Interventionen für sichere Systemansätze ermöglichen. Besonderes Augenmerk liegt auf Interaktionen zwischen Nutzern mit unterschiedlichen Massen und Geschwindigkeiten, darunter E-Bikes, E-Cargo-Bikes und E-Scooter für persönliche Mobilität und urbane Logistik. Große Piloten in vier europäischen Städten validieren Methoden im realen Verkehr, unterstützen das stadtübergreifende Lernen und gewährleisten die Anwendbarkeit unter verschiedenen Sicherheits-, Infrastruktur- und kulturellen Bedingungen. Implementiert von einem multidisziplinären Konsortium überbrücken Engineering, Verhaltenswissenschaften, XR, AI, Stadtplanung und Politik, bietet das Projekt handlungsfähige, standardisierte Anleitungen, die sicherere, inklusivere aktive und Mikromobilitätssysteme in ganz Europa beschleunigt. Die Planung sicherer städtischer Verkehrssysteme ist inhärent komplex: Eingreifen dauert seit Jahrzehnten, erfordert erhebliche Investitionen, muss in eingeschränkte Räume passen und muss ständig wechselnde Benutzerbedürfnisse erfüllen. Moderne Datenerfassungsmethoden, wie hochfrequente On-Board-Fahrzeugsensoren und Computer-Vision-Bilder, sind gut geeignet, diese Komplexitäten durch nahe Echtzeit-, hochauflösende Erkenntnisse zu erfassen. Das Sammeln, Bearbeiten und Betreiben dieser großen Datenvolumina ist jedoch eine Herausforderung durch heterogene Datenstrukturen und hohe Rechenanforderungen. Jobbeschreibung Diese Promotion zielt darauf ab, den Stand der Technik in der Sensor- und Fernerkundungsdatenfusion für die Sicherheitsanalyse der städtischen Verkehrsinfrastruktur voranzutreiben. Der Kandidat wird neue Tools und Methoden entwickeln, die Big Data, Computer Vision und maschinelles Lernen integrieren. Zu den Kernaufgaben des Kandidaten zählen:
• Entwickeln Sie eine skalierbare Sensing Pipeline: Entwerfen und implementieren Sie eine Software/Werkzeug-Architektur, die in der Lage ist, Mehrquellen-Fahrzeugsensor, Kamera und Fernerkundung Datenströme zu verarbeiten
• Automate Feature & Factor Identification: Train Machine Learning und Computer Vision-Modelle in der Pipeline, um die Eigenschaften der integrierten Umgebungsinfrastruktur und damit verbundene Faktoren zu erkennen, die die Sicherheit und den Komfort der Mikromobilität beeinflussen
• Mapping & Diagnostic Outputs generieren: Vergewissern Sie sich, dass die Software unterschiedliche Eingaben akzeptiert und strukturierte, qualitativ hochwertige Datenausgänge erzeugt, die für die räumliche Zuordnung, Risikodiagnose und nachgeschaltete Vorhersage-Sicherheitsmodellierung optimiert sind

descriptionByLocale.fr:
Poste de doctorat en analyse du capteur de véhicule et de la télédétection pour la sécurité routière 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Purée La chaire de gestion de l'infrastructure, dirigée par le professeur Bryan T. Adey à l'Institut de construction et de gestion de l'infrastructure du Département de génie civil, environnemental et géomatique, a une ouverture pour un doctorant. Cette position vise à tirer parti des capteurs de véhicules, de la télédétection et de l'apprentissage automatique pour soutenir l'analyse moderne de la sécurité routière urbaine dans le cadre d'un projet plus vaste de l'UE. Contexte du projet Le nouveau projet Horizon de l'UE favorise la mobilité active sûre et la recherche en introduisant une approche axée sur l'homme et fondée sur des données probantes qui intègre la sécurité réelle et perçue des piétons, des cyclistes et des utilisateurs de la micromobilité. Au-delà des approches conventionnelles axées sur les accidents, il capte les quasi-incidents, les interactions dynamiques et les expériences de sécurité incarnées qui façonnent le comportement et le choix du mode. Le projet combine des données multisources sur le trafic, l'infrastructure, les véhicules et la santé avec l'expérimentation immersive eXtended Reality (XR) et l'intelligence artificielle explicable pour analyser des situations critiques en matière de sécurité qui sont rares, sous-déclarées ou impossibles à observer sur le plan éthique dans le trafic réel. L'IA explicable assure la transparence et l'interprétation, appuyant la confiance, la transférabilité et la pertinence des politiques. Le projet traduit ces informations en méthodes d'évaluation harmonisées, en modèles de prévision et en indicateurs validés, permettant une évaluation et une comparaison solides des interventions réglementaires, infrastructurelles, technologiques et comportementales des parties prenantes à l'approche du système sûr. Une attention particulière est accordée aux interactions entre les utilisateurs avec des masses et des vitesses différentes, y compris les vélos électroniques, les vélos e-cargo et les e-cooters, pour la mobilité personnelle et la logistique urbaine. Des projets pilotes de grande envergure dans quatre villes européennes valident des méthodes de trafic réel, soutiennent l'apprentissage interurbain et garantissent leur applicabilité dans des conditions de sécurité, d'infrastructure et de culture diverses. Mis en œuvre par un consortium multidisciplinaire d'ingénierie, de science comportementale, de XR, d'IA, d'urbanisme et de politique, le projet fournit des orientations concrètes et standardisées qui accélèrent des systèmes actifs plus sûrs, plus inclusifs et de micromobilité dans toute l'Europe. La planification de systèmes de transport urbain sûrs est intrinsèquement complexe : les interventions durent des décennies, nécessitent des investissements importants, doivent s'adapter à des espaces restreints et doivent répondre à des besoins changeants des utilisateurs. Les méthodes modernes de collecte de données - telles que les capteurs de véhicules embarqués à haute fréquence et les images de vision par ordinateur - sont bien adaptées pour saisir ces complexités grâce à des aperçus à haute résolution en temps quasi réel. Cependant, la collecte, le traitement et l'opérationnalisation de ces volumes de mégadonnées sont un défi en raison de structures de données hétérogènes et de fortes demandes de calcul. Description de l'emploi Ce doctorat vise à faire progresser l'état de la technique en matière de fusion des données de détection et de télédétection pour l'analyse de la sécurité des infrastructures de transport urbain. Le candidat développera de nouveaux outils et méthodes qui intègrent les mégadonnées, la vision informatique et l'apprentissage automatique. Les principales tâches du candidat seront les suivantes :
• Développer un pipeline de détection évolutive : concevoir et mettre en œuvre une architecture logicielle/outil capable de traiter des flux de données multisources de capteurs, de caméras et de télédétection de véhicules
• Automatiser l'identification des caractéristiques et des facteurs: Train machine learning et les modèles de vision informatique dans le pipeline pour détecter automatiquement les caractéristiques de l'infrastructure bâtie et les facteurs connexes affectant la sécurité et le confort de la micromobilité
• Générer la cartographie et les sorties diagnostiques : s'assurer que le logiciel accepte divers intrants et génère des sorties de données structurées et de haute qualité optimisées pour la cartographie spatiale, le diagnostic des risques et la modélisation de la sécurité prédictive en aval
• Collaborer via Real-World Pilots: Valider et affiner le pipeline à l'aide de données réelles provenant des villes pilotes du projet, en travaillant en coope proche

jobs.description:
PhD Position in Infrastructure Intervention Effectiveness Analysis for Road Safety

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Infrastructure Management, led by Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey within the Institute of Construction and Infrastructure Management of the Department of Civil, Environmental, and Geomatic Engineering, has an opening for a PhD student. This position focuses on developing intervention effectiveness analysis methodologies to support urban road safety as a part of a larger EU project.

Project background

The new EU Horizon project advances safe active mobility uptake and research by introducing a human-centred, evidence-based approach that integrates actual and perceived safety for pedestrians, cyclists, and micromobility users. Moving beyond conventional crash-focused approaches, it captures near-misses, dynamic interactions, and embodied safety experiences that shape behaviour and mode choice. The project combines multi-source traffic, infrastructure, vehicle, and health data with immersive eXtended Reality (XR) experimentation and explainable Artificial Intelligence to analyse safety-critical situations that are rare, underreported, or ethically impossible to observe in real traffic. Explainable AI ensures transparency and interpretability, supporting trust, transferability, and policy relevance. The project translates these insights into harmonised assessment methodologies, predictive models, and validated indicators, enabling robust evaluation and comparison of regulatory, infrastructural, technological, and behavioural interventions across Safe System Approach stakeholders. Special focus is placed on interactions between users with differing masses and speeds, including e-bikes, e-cargo bikes, and e-scooters, for both personal mobility and urban logistics. Large-scale pilots in four European cities validate methods in real traffic, support cross-city learning, and ensure applicability under diverse safety, infrastructure and cultural conditions. Implemented by a multidisciplinary consortium bridging engineering, behavioural science, XR, AI, urban planning, and policy, the project delivers actionable, standardised guidance that accelerates safer, more inclusive active and micromobility systems across Europe.

Planning safe urban transport systems is inherently complex: interventions last for decades, have widespread impacts, require significant investment, must fit within constrained urban spaces, and must satisfy ever-changing, diverse user needs. Modern data collection and analysis methods are well-suited to capture these complexities by utilizing high-resolution data (e.g., high-frequency measurements from on-board vehicle sensors and computer-vision imagery) to provide near real-time insights. However, it is not yet clear how to effectively operationalize this data to identify high-risk areas, propose targeted infrastructure interventions, and measure their success - largely due to the relative novelty of these data sources, rapid vehicle advancements, and evolving urban mobility patterns.

Job description

This doctorate aims to advance the state-of-the-art in transport infrastructure safety analysis. Working closely with academic, industry, and public authority partners across Europe, the candidate’s core tasks will include:

• Structure Interventions: Structure and model potential infrastructure interventions designed to improve urban safety and comfort

• Develop Indicators: Create robust methodologies and indicators (e.g., surrogate safety measures) to evaluate intervention effectiveness in improving safety and comfort

• Real-World Validation: Apply and test developed frameworks across the project’s four European pilot cities, with a strong focus on the City of Zurich

• Consortium Collaboration: Coordinate regularly with local stakeholders, specifically Zurich’s Dienstabteilung Verkehr (DAV), and international project partners

Profile

• A Master’s degree i

PhD Posizione nell'Infrastruttura Analisi dell'efficacia dell'intervento per la sicurezza stradale 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo La Cattedra di Gestione delle Infrastrutture, guidata dal Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey all'interno dell'Istituto di Costruzione e Gestione delle Infrastrutture del Dipartimento di Ingegneria Civile, Ambientale e Geomatica, ha un'apertura per uno studente di dottorato. Questa posizione si concentra sullo sviluppo di metodologie di analisi dell'efficacia degli interventi per sostenere la sicurezza stradale urbana nell'ambito di un progetto UE più ampio. Sfondo del progetto Il nuovo progetto EU Horizon promuove l'assorbimento e la ricerca di una mobilità attiva sicura introducendo un approccio basato su prove umane che integra la sicurezza reale e percepita per pedoni, ciclisti e utenti di micromobilità. Passando oltre i convenzionali approcci focalizzati agli urti, cattura vicino-misses, interazioni dinamiche e esperienze di sicurezza incarnate che modellano il comportamento e la scelta della modalità. Il progetto combina il traffico multi-fonte, l'infrastruttura, il veicolo e i dati sanitari con la sperimentazione immersiva eXtended Reality (XR) e l'intelligenza artificiale spiegabile per analizzare situazioni di sicurezza-critical che sono rare, sottovalutate, o eticamente impossibili da osservare nel traffico reale. La Spiegabile AI garantisce trasparenza e interpretabilità, sostenendo fiducia, trasferibilità e rilevanza politica. Il progetto traduce queste intuizioni in metodologie di valutazione armonizzate, modelli predittivi e indicatori convalidati, consentendo una valutazione e un confronto robusti di interventi normativi, infrastrutturali, tecnologici e comportamentali tra gli stakeholder di Safe System Approach. Particolare attenzione è posta sulle interazioni tra utenti con diverse masse e velocità, tra cui e-bike, e-cargo bike, e-scooters, sia per la mobilità personale che per la logistica urbana. I piloti su larga scala in quattro città europee convalidano i metodi nel traffico reale, supportano l'apprendimento trasversale e garantiscono l'applicabilità in diverse condizioni di sicurezza, infrastruttura e cultura. Implementato da un'ingegneria multidisciplinare di collegamento consortile, scienza comportamentale, XR, AI, pianificazione urbana e politica, il progetto offre una guida attuabile e standardizzata che accelera sistemi attivi e di micromobilità più sicuri e inclusivi in tutta Europa. La pianificazione di sistemi di trasporto urbano sicuri è intrinsecamente complessa: gli interventi durano da decenni, hanno impatti molto diffusi, richiedono un investimento significativo, devono adattarsi all'interno di spazi urbani limitati, e devono soddisfare esigenze di utenti sempre mutevoli e diversificate. I moderni metodi di raccolta e analisi dei dati sono adatti per catturare queste complessità utilizzando dati ad alta risoluzione (ad esempio, misurazioni ad alta frequenza da sensori di veicolo on-board e immagini di computer-visione) per fornire approfondimenti in tempo reale. Tuttavia, non è ancora chiaro come operare efficacemente questi dati per identificare aree ad alto rischio, proporre interventi infrastrutturali mirati e misurare il loro successo - in gran parte a causa della relativa novità di queste fonti di dati, progressi rapidi del veicolo e modelli di mobilità urbana in evoluzione. Descrizione del lavoro Questo dottorato mira a promuovere lo stato dell'arte nell'analisi della sicurezza delle infrastrutture di trasporto. Lavorando a stretto contatto con partner accademici, industriali e di autorità pubbliche in tutta Europa, i compiti principali del candidato includono:
• Interventi Strutturali: Struttura e modelli potenziali interventi infrastrutturali volti a migliorare la sicurezza e il comfort urbano
• Sviluppare indicatori: creare metodologie e indicatori robusti (ad esempio, misure di sicurezza surrogate) per valutare l'efficacia degli interventi nel migliorare la sicurezza e il comfort
• Validazione Real-World: Applicare e testare i quadri sviluppati nelle quattro città pilota europee del progetto, con un forte focus sulla città di Zurigo
• Consorzio Collaborazione: Coordinate regolarmente con gli stakeholder locali, in particolare Dienstabteilung Verkehr (DAV) di Zurigo e partner internazionali di progetto Profilo
• Un master i

PhD-Position in der Infrastruktur Intervention Effektivitätsanalyse für Straßenverkehrssicherheit 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Der Lehrstuhl für Infrastrukturmanagement unter der Leitung von Prof. Dr. Bryan T. Adey im Institut für Bau- und Infrastrukturmanagement der Abteilung für Bau-, Umwelt- und Geotechnik hat eine Eröffnung für einen Doktoranden. Diese Position konzentriert sich auf die Entwicklung von Interventionseffektivitätsanalysemethoden zur Unterstützung der Straßenverkehrssicherheit im Rahmen eines größeren EU-Projekts. Projekt Hintergrund Das neue EU-Horizont-Projekt fördert die sichere aktive Mobilitätsaufnahme und -forschung durch die Einführung eines menschenzentrierten, evidenzbasierten Ansatzes, der die tatsächliche und wahrgenommene Sicherheit für Fußgänger, Radfahrer und Mikromobilitätsnutzer integriert. Über konventionelle Crash-fokussierte Ansätze hinweg zu bewegen, erfasst sie Nah-Maßnahmen, dynamische Interaktionen und verkörperte Sicherheitserlebnisse, die Verhalten und Moduswahl prägen. Das Projekt kombiniert Mehrquellen-Verkehrs-, Infrastruktur-, Fahrzeug- und Gesundheitsdaten mit immersiven eXtended Reality (XR)-Experimenten und erklärbaren künstlichen Intelligenzen, um sicherheitskritische Situationen zu analysieren, die selten, unterreportiert oder ethisch unmöglich sind, im realen Verkehr zu beobachten. Erklärbare KI sorgt für Transparenz und Dolmetschbarkeit, Unterstützung von Vertrauen, Übertragbarkeit und politischer Relevanz. Das Projekt übersetzt diese Erkenntnisse zu harmonisierten Bewertungsmethoden, Prädiktionsmodellen und validierten Indikatoren, die eine robuste Bewertung und Vergleich von regulatorischen, infrastrukturellen, technologischen und verhaltensbezogenen Interventionen für sichere Systemansätze ermöglichen. Besonderes Augenmerk liegt auf Interaktionen zwischen Nutzern mit unterschiedlichen Massen und Geschwindigkeiten, darunter E-Bikes, E-Cargo-Bikes und E-Scooter für persönliche Mobilität und urbane Logistik. Große Piloten in vier europäischen Städten validieren Methoden im realen Verkehr, unterstützen das stadtübergreifende Lernen und gewährleisten die Anwendbarkeit unter verschiedenen Sicherheits-, Infrastruktur- und kulturellen Bedingungen. Implementiert von einem multidisziplinären Konsortium überbrücken Engineering, Verhaltenswissenschaften, XR, AI, Stadtplanung und Politik, bietet das Projekt handlungsfähige, standardisierte Anleitungen, die sicherere, inklusivere aktive und Mikromobilitätssysteme in ganz Europa beschleunigt. Die Planung sicherer städtischer Verkehrssysteme ist inhärent komplex: die seit Jahrzehnten dauernden Interventionen haben weit verbreitete Auswirkungen, erfordern erhebliche Investitionen, müssen in eingeschränkte Stadträume passen und müssen ständig wechselnde, vielfältige Nutzerbedürfnisse erfüllen. Moderne Datenerfassungs- und Analysemethoden sind gut geeignet, diese Komplexitäten zu erfassen, indem hochauflösende Daten (z.B. hochfrequente Messungen von Bordfahrzeugsensoren und Computer-Vision-Bilder) verwendet werden, um nahe Echtzeit-Einsichten zu liefern. Es ist jedoch noch nicht klar, wie diese Daten effektiv zur Identifizierung von Hochrisikogebieten, zur Lösung gezielter Infrastrukturinterventionen und zur Messung ihres Erfolgs - vor allem aufgrund der relativen Neuheit dieser Datenquellen, der schnellen Fahrzeugfortschritte und der Entwicklung urbaner Mobilitätsmuster - eingesetzt werden können. Jobbeschreibung Diese Promotion zielt darauf ab, den Stand der Technik in der Verkehrsinfrastruktur-Sicherheitsanalyse voranzutreiben. In enger Zusammenarbeit mit Partnern aus Wissenschaft, Industrie und öffentlichen Behörden in ganz Europa werden die Kernaufgaben des Kandidaten umfassen:
• Strukturinterventionen: Struktur und Modell potenzielle Infrastrukturinterventionen zur Verbesserung der städtischen Sicherheit und des Komforts
• Entwicklung von Indikatoren: Erstellen Sie robuste Methoden und Indikatoren (z.B. überholte Sicherheitsmaßnahmen) zur Bewertung der Interventionseffizienz bei der Verbesserung von Sicherheit und Komfort
• Real-World Validation: Die vier europäischen Pilotstädte des Projekts mit einem starken Fokus auf die Stadt Zürich
• Consortium Collaboration: Koordinieren Sie regelmäßig mit lokalen Interessenvertretern, speziell der Dienstabteilung Verkehr Zürich (DAV) und internationalen Projektpartnern Profil

jobs.description:
PhD position in Multi-State Programmable Robotic Matter

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated PhD student to work on programmable materials that access multiple distinct mechanical states for next-generation robotic matter systems. This 4-year PhD position is fully funded.

Project background

Modern robots increasingly rely on sophisticated mechanisms, such as modular architectures, reconfigurable linkages, deployable structures, and variable-stiffness components, to adapt their bodies to different tasks and environments. However, such adaptability is often achieved by changing geometry, connectivity, or control strategies, while the underlying material properties remain largely fixed.

This project explores a more fundamental route: robotic matter whose constitutive properties can be programmed on demand. By enabling mechanical modulus, viscoelastic response, and flow behavior to be reconfigured within a single continuous body, we aim to move beyond adaptive hardware architectures towards materials that actively participate in robotic function. The long-term vision is to create robots that can tune their physical embodiment through the programmable properties of matter itself.

Job description

• Design, synthesis, and rheological characterization of dynamic covalent polymer composites targeting programmable mechanical state transitions

• Development of theoretical understanding and multiphysics simulation of material behavior across mechanical regimes

• Fabrication and integration of materials into soft robotic demonstrators showcasing multi-state control under external stimuli

• Development of spatial addressability strategies to achieve localized state modulation in a continuous material body

• Demonstration of robotic functions (locomotion, grasping, navigation through constrictions) that exploit multi-state material behavior

• Supervision of bachelor/master students and participation in teaching

This is a full-time position that starts as soon as possible. Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

descriptionByLocale.en:
PhD position in Multi-State Programmable Robotic Matter

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated PhD student to work on programmable materials that access multiple distinct mechanical states for next-generation robotic matter systems. This 4-year PhD position is fully funded.

Project background

Modern robots increasingly rely on sophisticated mechanisms, such as modular architectures, reconfigurable linkages, deployable structures, and variable-stiffness components, to adapt their bodies to different tasks and environments. However, such adaptability is often achieved by changing geometry, connectivity, or control strategies, while the underlying material properties remain largely fixed.

This project explores a more fundamental route: robotic matter whose constitutive properties can be programmed on demand. By enabling mechanical modulus, viscoelastic response, and flow behavior to be reconfigured within a single continuous body, we aim to move beyond adaptive hardware architectures towards materials that actively participate in robotic function. The long-term vision is to create robots that can tune their physical embodiment through the programmable properties of matter itself.

Job description

• Design, synthesis, and rheological characterization of dynamic covalent polymer composites targeting programmable mechanical state transitions

• Development of theoretical understanding and multiphysics simulation of material behavior across mechanical regimes

• Fabrication and integration of materials into soft robotic demonstrators showcasing multi-state control under external stimuli

• Development of spatial addressability strategies to achieve localized state modulation in a continuous material body

• Demonstration of robotic functions (locomotion, grasping, navigation through constrictions) that exploit multi-state material behavior

• Supervision of bachelor/master students and participation in teaching

This is a full-time position that starts as soon as possible. Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Profile

• MS degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Polymer Chemistry, Mechanical Engineering, or related fields from a leading university

• Strong research track record in one or more of the following: dynamic covalent networks, phase-change materials, rheology of complex materials, stimuli-responsive polymers, or soft robotics

• Enthusiasm for fundamental materials challenges with a drive toward robotic applications

• Excellent problem-solving abilities and comfort with interdisciplinary work spanning chemistry, mechanics, and robotics

• Experience with polymer synthesis, mechanical testing, or material fabrication is a strong plus

jobs.description:
PhD position in Biohybrid Robotics

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

Build the next generation of muscle-actuated robots in a lab whose recent biohybrid work has been published in Science Advances and Advanced Intelligent Systems.

The Soft Robotics Lab within the Institute of Robotics and Intelligent Systems at ETH Zurich is inviting applications for an open doctoral position. We are looking for an excellent researcher to join and advance our research efforts in the fabrication and control of biohybrid robots. Our lab's goal is to build, model, and control robots in a fundamentally different way, so that they become more flexible, dexterous, capable, and adapt better to their environment. On the biohybrid side, the lab has recently demonstrated 3D-bioprinted muscle-tendon interfaces with enhanced force transmission (Science Advances, 2025) and sensor-embedded muscle enabling closed-loop proprioceptive control (Advanced Intelligent Systems, 2025), work that has been featured in ETH press and international robotics media.

Project background

The frontier of research in soft robotics aims at replacing classic soft materials used for actuators with biological ones (muscle) to take advantage of the innate adaptability, energy efficiency, and softness of biological systems. While a few years ago these biohybrid robots (bio-bots) could be considered a matter for science fiction, recent work has demonstrated fish-like swimming bio-bots, caterpillar-like walking bio-bots, and even pick-and-place biological machines powered by engineered muscle tissue.

Within this research area, the SRL designs, fabricates, and characterizes muscle-driven biohybrid robots. Muscle constructs are produced using hydrogel casting, micro-molding, and light- and extrusion-based bioprinting, then actuated through electrical stimulation and analyzed via motion tracking. Current research challenges include scaling up engineered muscle tissues, controlling myofiber formation during biofabrication and maturation, exploring tissue architectures from biomimetic to biosynthetic forms, integrating proprioception into muscle-based actuators, and discovering sustainable materials for biohybrid systems (including non-mammalian sources).

Recent results from the lab include muscle–tendon bioprinting of mechanically optimized musculoskeletal bioactuators with enhanced force transmission (Filippi et al., Science Advances, 2025); sensor-embedded muscle for closed-loop, proprioceptive control of biohybrid robots (Filippi et al., Advanced Intelligent Systems, 2025); perfusable bioprinted skeletal muscle tissue at the centimeter scale (Filippi et al., Advanced Healthcare Materials, 2023); a perspective on microfluidics for functionally integrated biohybrid robots (Filippi et al., PNAS, 2022); and bilayered biofabrication unlocking skeletal muscle for biohybrid soft robots (Balciunaite et al., RoboSoft, 2024).

The doctoral candidate will join an interdisciplinary team working at the intersection of tissue engineering, biofabrication, robotics, and control. Day-to-day mentorship will come from senior biohybrid researchers in the lab, including Miriam Filippi and Aiste Balciunaite, both co-authors on the works cited above. Cross-group collaborations within ETH Zurich and active international collaborations with IBEC Barcelona (Sanchez, Guix), the University of Tokyo (Takeuchi), and Empa (Clemens) are part of the day-to-day research environment.

Doctoral candidates will be employed according to the regulations of ETH Zurich, and upon completing the doctorate, will be awarded the title "Doctor of Sciences (Dr. sc. ETH Zurich)". More information about the ETH Zurich doctorate can be found here .

The thesis work will focus on:

• Designing and engineering bioreactors for the mechanical tensioning, electrical stimulation, and long-term maturation of engineered muscle constructs

• Bioprinting of complex muscle architectures using extrusion- and ligh

PhD posizione in Biohybrid Robotics 100%, Zurigo, contratto a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Descrizione Costruire la generazione prossima di robot attuati da pazienti in un laboratorio il cui lavoro bioibrido recente è stato pubblicato in Science Advances e Advanced Intelligent Systems. Il Laboratorio di Robotica Soft all'interno dell'Istituto di Robotica e Sistemi Intelligenti dell'ETH Zurigo invita le candidature per una posizione aperta di dottorato. Cerchiamo un eccellente ricercatore per unirsi e avanzare i nostri sforzi di ricerca nella produzione e controllo di robot bioibridi. L'obiettivo del nostro laboratorio è costruire, modellare e controllare i robot in un modo oscuro, in modo che diventanono più flessibili, agili, capaci e adattabili all'ambiente. Dal lato bioibrido, il laboratorio ha recentemente dimostrato muscolo-tendine 3D-bioprintate con trasmissione di forza migliorata (Science Advances, 2025) e pazienti sensorizzati che permettono il controllo proprioceutivo a chiusura (Advanced Intelligent Systems, 2025), lavoro che è stato presentato nella stampa ETH e nei media internazionali di robotica. Contesto del progetto La frontiera della ricerca in robotica soft mira a sostituire i classici materiali morbo utilizzati per gli attuatori con quelli biologici (muscoli) per sfruttare l'adattabilità innata, l'efficienza energetica e la morbidezza dei sistemi biologici. Quando pochi anni fa robot bioibridi (bio-bots) potrebbero essere considerati una questione di fantascienza, il lavoro recente ha mostrato bio-bots che nuotano come pesci, camminano come formiche e persino macchine biologiche per la raccolta e il posizionamento potenziate da tessuti ingegnerizzati. All'interno di questa area di ricerca, lo pianificazione SRL, fabbrica e caratterizza robot bioibridi attuati da motori. I costrutti vengono prodotti utilizzando la stampa a gel di idrogel, la micro-molding e la bioprinting a luce e extrusione, poi attuati attraverso la stimolazione elettrica e analizzati tramite la tracciatura del movimento. Le attuali sfide di ricerca includono la scalabilità dei tessuti ingegnerizzati, il controllo della formazione dei miofibri durante la biofabbricazione e la maturazione, l'esplorazione delle architetture tessutali da biomimetico a biosintetico, l'integrazione della propriocezione negli attuatori basati su rischi e la scoperta di materiali sostenibili per i sistemi bioibridi (compresi fonti non mammiliane). I risultati recenti del laboratorio comprendono la bioprinting muscolo-tendine per attuatori muscolo-scheletrici bioibridi ottimizzati meccanicamente con trasmissione di forza migliorata (Filippi et sui., Science Advances, 2025); pazienti sensorizzati per il controllo proprioceuridi a chiusura dei robot bioibridi (Filippi efabbricat al., Advanced Intelligent Systems, 2025); tessuti correlati scheletrico bioprintcafluppi a scala Requisiti Il candidato dovrà un team interdisciplinare che lavora all'intersezione dell'ingegneria tessutale, della biofabbricazione, della robotica e del controllo. La guida viene fornita da ricerca senior bioibridi nel laboratorio, compresi Miriam Filippi e Aiste Balciunaite, entrambi coautori dei lavori citati sopra. Le collaborazioni incrociate all'interno dell'ETH Zurigo e le collaborazioni internazionali attive con IBEC Barcelona (Sanchez, Guix), l'Università di Tokyo (Takeuchi) e Empa (Clemens) fanno parte dell'ambiente di ricerca quotidiano. Cosa? I candidati devono essere impiegati secondo le norme dell'ETH Zurigo, e dopo aver completato il dottorato, saranno insigniti del titolo di "Dottore delle Scienze (Dr. sc. ETH Zurigo)". • Bioprinting di architetture complesse utilizzando l'extrusione e la bioprinting a luce
• Controllo elettro-muscolare dei robot bioibridi
• Sviluppo di materiali sostenibili per i sistemi bioibridi

jobs.description:
PhD position in Soft Robotics Systems

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Soft Robotics Lab within the Institute of Robotics and Intelligent Systems at ETH Zurich is inviting applications for an open doctoral position. We are looking for an exceptional, hands-on engineer to design, build, and bring to life the next generation of artificial musculoskeletal robots. Our lab's goal is to build, model, and control robots in a fundamentally different way, so that they become more flexible, dexterous, capable, and adapt better to their environment. The lab has showcased its research in robotic design and algorithms through real-world applications such as a robotic fish for underwater locomotion , soft robotic hands for pick-and-place tasks , and multi-segment arms for dynamic object manipulation.

Project background

Today’s robots are mostly rigid, fragile, and a world apart from the agility and resilience of biological bodies. We believe the path to capable, safe, and lifelike machines runs through musculoskeletal soft robots: systems built from compliant structures, bones, joints, and tendon-like actuation, much like the bodies of animals and humans. As a PhD researcher in our group, you will lead the design, fabrication, and real-world testing of these robots end to end, turning ideas into working hardware that moves, grasps, and interacts with the physical world.

This is a builder’s role at its core. You will work across mechanical design, soft and compliant actuation, fabrication, electronics, and control to create complete robotic systems, then iterate relentlessly through hands-on experimentation until they perform in the real world. Our recent work, from a biohybrid bone-muscle interface that gives robots real muscles and tendons to a robotic fish, dexterous soft hands, and dynamic manipulator arms, reflects the kind of ambitious, physical research you would be joining.

Job description

• You will take musculoskeletal soft robots from concept to working prototype: conceiving the architecture, designing and fabricating the structural and actuation elements, integrating sensing and control, and validating performance through systematic real-world testing

• Each design cycle feeds the next, so rapid prototyping, measurement, and iteration sit at the heart of the project

• Drawing inspiration from biological musculoskeletal systems, you will engineer how bones, joints, tendons, and muscles can be recreated with compliant materials and actuators, and how their interplay produces strength, dexterity, and robustness

• The goal is to build robots that derive much of their capability from their embodiment, achieving rich, adaptive behavior with less reliance on complex centralized control

• You will combine hands-on mechanical design, fabrication, and experimental testing with modeling, actuation, and control to deliver complete, functional robots, ranging from single actuated joints to integrated multi-segment limbs and full musculoskeletal bodies

• Close, day-to-day collaboration with the lab’s machine learning team and its muscles team will be required and is key to the project: you will integrate learning-based control and sensing with the team’s biological and artificial muscle technology to build robots that no single discipline could achieve alone

Profile

You are extremely curious, highly motivated, greatly independent, and you want to make a real difference with your research. You work best when you are in a team, you are respectful and thrive when you can collaborate with others and provide support. Through your prior experiences, you have ideally already shown your understanding and skills in:

• Master’s degree in mechanical engineering, robotics, mechatronics, electrical engineering, or a closely related field

• Demonstrated hands-on experience building physical systems: prototyping, CAD, fabrication (e.g. 3D printing, machining, molding), electronics, or robot integration
