Posizione di dottorato in Sistemi di Robotica Morbida 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il Soft Robotics Lab all'interno dell'Istituto di Robotica e Sistemi Intelligenti dell'ETH di Zurigo invita le applicazioni per una posizione di dottorato aperta. Siamo alla ricerca di un ingegnere mani-on eccezionale per progettare, costruire e portare alla vita la prossima generazione di robot muscoloscheletrici artificiali. L'obiettivo del nostro laboratorio è quello di costruire, modellare e controllare i robot in modo fondamentalmente diverso, in modo che diventino più flessibili, dexterous, capaci, e si adattano meglio al loro ambiente. Il laboratorio ha messo in mostra la sua ricerca nel design robotico e negli algoritmi attraverso applicazioni del mondo reale come un pesce robotico per locomozione subacquea, mani robotiche morbide per compiti pick-and-place e braccia multi-segment per la manipolazione dinamica degli oggetti. Sfondo del progetto I robot di oggi sono per lo più rigidi, fragili e un mondo a parte l'agilità e la resilienza dei corpi biologici. Crediamo che il percorso di macchine capaci, sicure e realistiche avvenga attraverso robot molli muscoloschelettrici: sistemi costruiti da strutture conformi, ossa, articolazioni e attuazione simile al tendine, molto simile ai corpi di animali e umani. Come ricercatore di dottorato nel nostro gruppo, guiderai la progettazione, la fabbricazione e il test del mondo reale di questi robot finiscono per finire, trasformando le idee in hardware funzionante che si muove, afferra e interagisce con il mondo fisico. Questo è il ruolo di un costruttore al suo nucleo. Potrai lavorare attraverso la progettazione meccanica, l'attuazione morbida e conforme, la fabbricazione, l'elettronica e il controllo per creare sistemi robotici completi, quindi iterare incessantemente attraverso la sperimentazione pratica fino a quando non si esibiscono nel mondo reale. Il nostro recente lavoro, da un'interfaccia bioibrida ossea-muscolo che dà robot muscoli reali e tendini a un pesce robotico, mani morbide dexterose e braccia manipolatrici dinamiche, riflette il tipo di ricerca fisica ambiziosa che si unirebbe. Descrizione del lavoro
• Prenderai robot morbidi muscoloschelettrici dal concept al prototipo di lavoro: concepire l'architettura, progettare e fabbricare gli elementi strutturali e attuativi, integrando il rilevamento e il controllo, e convalidando le prestazioni attraverso test sistematici del mondo reale
• Ogni ciclo di progettazione alimenta il prossimo, così rapido prototipazione, misurazione e iterazione siedono al cuore del progetto
• Traendo ispirazione da sistemi muscoloschelettrici biologici, si ingegnerà come ossa, articolazioni, tendini e muscoli possono essere ricreati con materiali e attuatori conformi, e come il loro gioco produce forza, destrezza e robustezza
• L'obiettivo è quello di costruire robot che derivano gran parte della loro capacità dall'incarnazione, ottenendo un comportamento ricco e adattativo con meno dipendenza dal controllo centralizzato complesso
• Combinate la progettazione meccanica, la fabbricazione e i test sperimentali con la modellazione, l'attuazione e il controllo per fornire robot completi e funzionali, che vanno da singole articolazioni attuate a arti multisegment integrati e corpi muscoloschelettrici completi
• Una stretta collaborazione quotidiana con il team di apprendimento automatico del laboratorio e il suo team di muscoli sarà richiesto ed è fondamentale per il progetto: si integra il controllo basato sull’apprendimento e la percezione con la tecnologia muscolare biologica e artificiale del team per costruire robot che nessuna singola disciplina potrebbe raggiungere da solo Profilo Siete estremamente curiosi, altamente motivati, molto indipendenti, e si desidera fare una vera differenza con la vostra ricerca. Si lavora meglio quando si è in una squadra, si è rispettosi e prosperare quando è possibile collaborare con gli altri e fornire supporto. Attraverso le vostre esperienze precedenti, avete idealmente già mostrato la vostra comprensione e competenze in:
• Laurea magistrale in ingegneria meccanica, robotica, meccatronica, ingegneria elettrica o un campo strettamente correlato
• Sistemi fisici per la costruzione di esperienze dimostrate: prototipazione, CAD, fabbricazione (ad esempio stampa 3D, lavorazione, stampaggio), integrazione elettronica o robot

PhD Position in Soft Robotics Systems 100%, Zürich, befristet Druck Druckerzeugnisse Das Soft Robotics Lab des Instituts für Robotik und Intelligente Systeme der ETH Zürich lädt zur Bewerbung um eine offene Doktorandenstelle ein. Wir suchen einen außergewöhnlichen, praktischen Ingenieur, der die nächste Generation künstlicher Muskel-Skelett-Roboter entwerfen, bauen und zum Leben erwecken kann. Ziel unseres Labors ist es, Roboter grundlegend anders zu bauen, zu modellieren und zu steuern, so dass sie flexibler, geschickter, fähiger werden und sich besser an ihre Umgebung anpassen. Das Labor hat seine Forschung im Bereich Roboterdesign und Algorithmen durch reale Anwendungen wie einen Roboterfisch für die Unterwasserbewegung, weiche Roboterhände für Pick-and-Place-Aufgaben und Multisegmentarme für die dynamische Objektmanipulation vorgestellt. Projekthintergrund Heutige Roboter sind meist starr, zerbrechlich und eine Welt abseits der Agilität und Widerstandsfähigkeit biologischer Körper. Wir glauben, dass der Weg zu fähigen, sicheren und lebensechten Maschinen durch muskuloskelettale weiche Roboter verläuft: Systeme, die aus nachgiebigen Strukturen, Knochen, Gelenken und sehnenähnlicher Betätigung aufgebaut sind, ähnlich wie die Körper von Tieren und Menschen. Als PhD-Forscher in unserer Gruppe leiten Sie das Design, die Herstellung und das reale Testen dieser Roboter Ende an Ende und verwandeln Ideen in funktionierende Hardware, die sich bewegt, erfasst und mit der physischen Welt interagiert. Dies ist die Rolle eines Erbauers in seinem Kern. Sie werden über mechanisches Design, weiche und konforme Betätigung, Fertigung, Elektronik und Steuerung arbeiten, um vollständige Robotersysteme zu erstellen, und dann unerbittlich durch praktische Experimente iterieren, bis sie in der realen Welt funktionieren. Unsere jüngsten Arbeiten, von einer biohybriden Knochen-Muskel-Schnittstelle, die Robotern echte Muskeln und Sehnen zu einem Roboterfisch, geschickten weichen Händen und dynamischen Manipulatorarmen gibt, spiegeln die Art von ehrgeiziger, physischer Forschung wider, der Sie beitreten würden. Stellenbeschreibung
• Sie werden muskuloskelettale weiche Roboter vom Konzept zum funktionierenden Prototyp bringen: Konzeption der Architektur, Entwurf und Herstellung der Struktur- und Betätigungselemente, Integration von Sensorik und Steuerung und Validierung der Leistung durch systematische reale Tests Jeder Entwurfszyklus füttert den nächsten, so dass Rapid Prototyping, Messung und Iteration im Mittelpunkt des Projekts stehen.
• Indem Sie sich von biologischen Muskel-Skelett-Systemen inspirieren lassen, entwickeln Sie, wie Knochen, Gelenke, Sehnen und Muskeln mit nachgiebigen Materialien und Aktoren nachgebildet werden können und wie ihr Zusammenspiel Kraft, Geschicklichkeit und Robustheit erzeugt Ziel ist es, Roboter zu bauen, die einen Großteil ihrer Fähigkeiten aus ihrer Verkörperung ableiten und ein reiches, adaptives Verhalten mit weniger Abhängigkeit von komplexer zentralisierter Steuerung erreichen.
• Sie kombinieren praktisches mechanisches Design, Fertigung und experimentelle Tests mit Modellierung, Betätigung und Steuerung, um vollständige, funktionale Roboter zu liefern, die von einzelnen betätigten Gelenken bis hin zu integrierten Multisegment-Gliedern und vollständigen Muskel-Skelett-Körpern reichen Eine enge, tägliche Zusammenarbeit mit dem maschinellen Lernteam des Labors und seinem Muskelteam ist erforderlich und der Schlüssel zum Projekt: Sie integrieren lernbasierte Steuerung und Sensorik mit der biologischen und künstlichen Muskeltechnologie des Teams, um Roboter zu bauen, die keine einzelne Disziplin alleine erreichen könnte Profil Sie sind extrem neugierig, hoch motiviert, sehr unabhängig und möchten mit Ihrer Forschung einen echten Unterschied machen. Sie arbeiten am besten, wenn Sie in einem Team sind, Sie sind respektvoll und gedeihen, wenn Sie mit anderen zusammenarbeiten und Unterstützung bieten können. • Demonstrierte praktische Erfahrung beim Bau physischer Systeme: Prototyping, CAD, Fertigung (z. B. 3D-Druck, Bearbeitung, Formgebung), Elektronik oder Roboterintegration

Doctorat en Systèmes de Robotique Douce 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le Soft Robotics Lab de l'Institut de Robotique et de Systèmes Intelligents de Zurich invite les candidats à un poste de doctorat ouvert. Nous sommes à la recherche d'un ingénieur exceptionnel et pratique pour concevoir, construire et donner vie à la prochaine génération de robots musculosquelettiques artificiels. Le but de notre laboratoire est de construire, de modéliser et de contrôler des robots d'une manière fondamentalement différente, afin qu'ils deviennent plus flexibles, dextérieux, capables et s'adaptent mieux à leur environnement. Le laboratoire a présenté ses recherches en conception robotique et en algorithmes à travers des applications du monde réel telles qu'un poisson robotisé pour la locomotion sous-marine, des mains robotiques douces pour les tâches de pick-and-place, et des bras multi-segments pour la manipulation dynamique d'objets. Contexte du projet Aujourd'hui, les robots sont pour la plupart rigides, fragiles et un monde à part l'agilité et la résilience des corps biologiques. Nous croyons que le chemin vers des machines capables, sûres et qui ressemblent à une vie passe par des robots mous musculosquelettiques : des systèmes construits à partir de structures, d'os, de articulations et d'actionnements semblables à des tendons, tout comme les corps des animaux et des humains. En tant que doctorant au sein de notre groupe, vous dirigerez la conception, la fabrication et les essais sur le monde réel de ces robots se terminent par la transformation des idées en matériel de travail qui bouge, saisit et interagit avec le monde physique. Il s'agit d'un rôle de constructeur à son cœur. Vous travaillerez à travers la conception mécanique, l'actionnement souple et conforme, la fabrication, l'électronique et le contrôle pour créer des systèmes robotiques complets, puis itérer sans relâche par l'expérimentation pratique jusqu'à ce qu'ils se produisent dans le monde réel. Notre travail récent, à partir d'une interface osseux-muscle biohybride qui donne aux robots de véritables muscles et tendons à un poisson robotisé, des mains douces dextérieuses et des bras manipulateurs dynamiques, reflète le genre de recherche physique ambitieuse que vous joindrez. Description du poste
• Vous prendrez des robots mous musculosquelettiques du concept au prototype de travail: concevoir l'architecture, concevoir et fabriquer les éléments structuraux et d'action, intégrer la détection et le contrôle, et valider les performances par des tests systématiques du monde réel
• Chaque cycle de conception alimente le prochain, si rapide prototypage, mesure et itération sont au cœur du projet

jobs.description:
Senior Storage & Data Engineer

80%-100%, Lugano, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) develops and operates a high-performance computing and data research infrastructure that supports world-class science in Switzerland. Its user laboratory is available to domestic and international researchers in academia, industry, and the business sector. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices at its data centre in Lugano and in Zurich.

For this position the work location is either Lugano or Zürich. The contract is for two years.

Project background

Storing petabytes is the easy part. The hard part is everything between the moment data lands on disk and the moment a researcher — or a training job — can actually trust it, find it, and use it.

Our parallel filesystems and object stores already move data fast. What they don't do on their own is tell a scientist where a dataset came from, which transformations produced it, whether it's the version that backed last quarter's published result, or how to feed it to a DataLoader without saturating the I/O subsystem. That gap — between raw bytes and usable, traceable, reproducible data — is where this role lives.

You'll work at both ends: the storage layer (throughput, integrity, tiering at multi-petabyte scale) and the data layer above it (lineage, provenance, discoverability, access patterns). If you've ever been annoyed that "the data is on the cluster" gets treated as the end of the job rather than the start of it, read on.

Job description

• Bridge ingestion and use. Design the pipelines and metadata that turn ingested data into something findable and consumable — catalogs, schemas, and access layers that match how training jobs and simulations actually read, not just where bytes sit.

• Make data traceable. Build lineage and provenance so any dataset, checkpoint, or result can be traced back to its inputs and transformations. Reproducibility is a first-class requirement here, not a retrofit.

• Tune for the workload. Optimise parallel filesystems (Lustre, GPFS) and object storage for the concurrency, small-file, and large-checkpoint patterns of distributed GPU training and HPC simulation.

• Operate at scale, safely. Design and run multi-petabyte storage with the integrity and availability scientific work depends on — erasure coding, redundancy, hot-to-archival tiering.

• Automate everything. Deploy and scale storage and data services as code. Snowflake infrastructure doesn't survive at this scale.

• Make it observable. Instrument storage health, capacity trends, and pipeline performance so problems surface before users feel them.

• Translate. Turn real access patterns from domain scientists and ML engineers into technical requirements — and push back when a request would quietly break something downstream.

For a project in the weather and climate domain, aimed at understanding and mitigating the impact of climate change, an opening for two years is available.

The initial two-year contract could potentially be extended or even become permanent.

Profile

• A technical degree (CS, engineering) or equivalent experience that demonstrates the same depth.

• Solid storage grounding: filesystems (block and object), performance tuning, redundancy (RAID, erasure coding).

• Python, and comfort automating infrastructure (Ansible, Terraform, or similar).

• A working understanding of how ML and scientific workloads consume data — billions of small files, large checkpoints, sharding — and why naive layouts fall over.

• A point of view on data lineage, provenance, or reproducibility — and ideally tooling you've used to enforce it.

What helps you stand out

• Hands-on parallel filesystems (Lustre, Spectrum Scale/GPFS) or distributed storage (Ceph, VAST).

• Scientific data formats — HDF5, Zarr, Parquet — and opinions on when each earns its place.

• Object storage (S3

descriptionByLocale.it:
Senior Storage & Data Engineer 80%-100%, Lugano, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Lo Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) sviluppa e gestisce un'infrastruttura di calcolo e di ricerca dati ad alte prestazioni che supporta la scienza di livello mondiale in Svizzera. Il suo laboratorio di utenti è disponibile per i ricercatori nazionali e internazionali in accademia, industria e settore business. Il centro è gestito da ETH Zurich e ha sede presso il suo data center di Lugano e a Zurigo. Per questa posizione la posizione di lavoro è Lugano o Zurigo. Il contratto è per due anni. Sfondo del progetto Memorizzare i petabyte è la parte facile. La parte difficile è tutto tra il momento in cui i dati atterrano su disco e il momento in cui un ricercatore — o un lavoro di formazione — può effettivamente fidarsi, trovarlo, e usarlo. I nostri filesystem paralleli e i negozi di oggetti già spostano i dati velocemente. Ciò che non fanno da soli è dire a uno scienziato da cui proviene un dataset, da cui le trasformazioni lo hanno prodotto, se è la versione che ha supportato il risultato pubblicato dello scorso trimestre, o come alimentarlo a un DataLoader senza saturare il sottosistema I/O. Questo divario — tra byte grezze e dati utilizzabili, tracciabili, riproducibili — è dove vive questo ruolo. Potrai lavorare a entrambe le estremità: lo strato di archiviazione (throughput, integrità, tiering a scala multipetabyte) e lo strato di dati sopra di esso (linea, provenienza, scoperta, modelli di accesso). Se sei mai stato infastidito che "i dati sono sul cluster" viene trattato come la fine del lavoro piuttosto che l'inizio di esso, leggere. Descrizione del lavoro
• Ingestione del ponte e uso. Progettare le tubazioni e i metadati che trasformano i dati ingestibili in qualcosa di rintracciabile e consumabile — cataloghi, schemi e livelli di accesso che corrispondono a come i lavori di formazione e le simulazioni effettivamente leggono, non solo dove i byte siedono.
• Rendere tracciabili i dati. Costruisci lignaggio e la provenienza in modo che qualsiasi dataset, checkpoint o risultato possano essere ricondotti ai suoi input e trasformazioni. La reproducibilità è un requisito di prima classe qui, non un retrofit.
• Singolo per il carico di lavoro. Ottimizzare i filesystem paralleli (Lustre, GPFS) e lo storage degli oggetti per la convalutazione, i piccoli file e i modelli di grande controllo della formazione GPU distribuita e della simulazione HPC.
• Operare in scala, in modo sicuro. Progettare ed eseguire lo storage multi-petabyte con l'integrità e la disponibilità di lavoro scientifico dipende da — la codifica di cancellazione, ridondanza, tiering caldo-architettonico.
• Automatizzare tutto. Distribuire e scalare i servizi di archiviazione e dati come codice. L'infrastruttura dei fiocchi di neve non sopravvive a questa scala.
• Renderlo osservabile. Sanità di stoccaggio dello strumento, tendenze di capacità e prestazioni di pipeline così i problemi si estendono prima che gli utenti li sentano.
• Traduci. Trasformare modelli di accesso reale da scienziati di dominio e ingegneri ML in requisiti tecnici - e spingere indietro quando una richiesta avrebbe tranquillamente rompere qualcosa a valle. Per un progetto nel campo del clima e del clima, finalizzato alla comprensione e alla mitigazione dell'impatto del cambiamento climatico, è disponibile un'apertura per due anni. descriptionByLocale.en:
Senior Storage & Data Engineer

80%-100%, Lugano, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) develops and operates a high-performance computing and data research infrastructure that supports world-class science in Switzerland. Its user laboratory is available to domestic and international researchers in academia, industry, and the business sector. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices at its data centre in Lugano and in Zurich.

For this position the work location is either Lugano or Zürich. The contract is for two years.

Project background

Storing petabytes is the easy part. The hard part is everything between the moment data lands on disk and the moment a researcher — or a training job — can actually trust it, find it, and use it.

Our parallel filesystems and object stores already move data fast. What they don't do on their own is tell a scientist where a dataset came from, which transformations produced it, whether it's the version that backed last quarter's published result, or how to feed it to a DataLoader without saturating the I/O subsystem. That gap — between raw bytes and usable, traceable, reproducible data — is where this role lives.

You'll work at both ends: the storage layer (throughput, integrity, tiering at multi-petabyte scale) and the data layer above it (lineage, provenance, discoverability, access patterns). If you've ever been annoyed that "the data is on the cluster" gets treated as the end of the job rather than the start of it, read on.

Job description

• Bridge ingestion and use. Design the pipelines and metadata that turn ingested data into something findable and consumable — catalogs, schemas, and access layers that match how training jobs and simulations actually read, not just where bytes sit.

• Make data traceable. Build lineage and provenance so any dataset, checkpoint, or result can be traced back to its inputs and transformations. Reproducibility is a first-class requirement here, not a retrofit.

• Tune for the workload. Optimise parallel filesystems (Lustre, GPFS) and object storage for the concurrency, small-file, and large-checkpoint patterns of distributed GPU training and HPC simulation.

• Operate at scale, safely. Design and run multi-petabyte storage with the integrity and availability scientific work depends on — erasure coding, redundancy, hot-to-archival tiering.

• Automate everything. Deploy and scale storage and data services as code. Snowflake infrastructure doesn't survive at this scale.

• Make it observable. Instrument storage health, capacity trends, and pipeline performance so problems surface before users feel them.

• Translate. Turn real access patterns from domain scientists and ML engineers into technical requirements — and push back when a request would quietly break something downstream.

For a project in the weather and climate domain, aimed at understanding and mitigating the impact of climate change, an opening for two years is available.

The initial two-year contract could potentially be extended or even become permanent.

Profile

• A technical degree (CS, engineering) or equivalent experience that demonstrates the same depth.

• Solid storage grounding: filesystems (block and object), performance tuning, redundancy (RAID, erasure coding).

• Python, and comfort automating infrastructure (Ansible, Terraform, or similar).

• A working understanding of how ML and scientific workloads consume data — billions of small files, large checkpoints, sharding — and why naive layouts fall over.

• A point of view on data lineage, provenance, or reproducibility — and ideally tooling you've used to enforce it.

What helps you stand out

• Hands-on parallel filesystems (Lustre, Spectrum Scale/GPFS) or distributed storage (Ceph, VAST).

• Scientific data formats — HDF5, Zarr, Parquet — and opinions on when each earns its place.

• Object storage (S3

• Une compréhension pratique de la façon dont les charges de travail et les charges de travail scientifiques consomment des données — des milliards de petits fichiers, de grands points de contrôle, de l'ardeur — et de la raison pour laquelle les plans naïfs tombent.

Hochschulabsolvent:in der Sozialwissenschaften an der Dozentur Militärsoziologie (m/w/d)

80%, Zürich, befristet

print
Drucken

Die Militärakademie (MILAK) an der ETH Zürich ist das Kompetenzzentrum für Militärwissenschaften und die Aus- und Weiterbildungsstätte für Berufsoffiziere. Forschungsschwerpunkte der Dozentur Militärsoziologie sind die Auseinandersetzung mit dem Schweizer Milizsystem, die internationale Streitkräfteentwicklung und die zivil-militärischen Beziehungen

Projekthintergrund

In Zusammenarbeit mit dem Center for Security Studies (CSS) der ETH Zürich wird jährlich die Studie «Sicherheit» durchgeführt und erhebt die aussen-, sicherheits- und verteidigungspolitische Meinungsbildung der Schweizer Stimmbevölkerung.

Stellenbeschreibung

Als Mitautor:in der Studie «Sicherheit 2027» unterstützen Sie die Dozentur Militärsoziologie beim Publikationsprozess (Datenerhebung, Datenauswertung, Verfassen von Kapiteln und Zusammenfassungen, Medienarbeit). Neben der Mitarbeit an diesem Forschungsprojekt werden kleinere Arbeiten für die Dozentur anfallen.

Profil

Sie sind Sozialwissenschaftler:in (vorzugsweise mit Abschluss in Soziologie oder Politikwissenschaften), verfügen über gute Kenntnisse der quantitativen empirischen Sozialforschung und bringen Interesse an Meinungsumfragen, Sicherheitspolitik und Militärsoziologie mit. Sie sind versiert in der statistischen Datenauswertung mit R und im Umgang mit den gängigen Office-Programmen und haben ausgezeichnete Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift. Sehr gute Sprachkenntnisse in Französisch sind von Vorteil. Die Stelle ist als Förderung für junge Akademiker/innen gedacht. Deshalb dürfen Ihr Studienabschluss und der Arbeitsbeginn höchstens 18 Monate auseinanderliegen.

Arbeitsort

Wir bieten

Die Dozentur Militärsoziologie besteht aus einem jungen Team, das eine rege, internationale Forschungstätigkeit aufweist. Ihr Arbeitsplatz befindet sich in Birmensdorf ZH, Kaserne Reppischtal.
Der Stellenantritt erfolgt per 01.10.2026 oder nach Vereinbarung bis 30.06.2027.

Neugierig? Sind wir auch.

Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Online-Bewerbung mit den folgenden Unterlagen:

• CV

• Motivationsschreiben

• Arbeitszeugnisse & Diplome (Leistungsnachweis des Studiums)

Bitte senden Sie Ihre Bewerbung an lic. phil. MAS in Criminology (LL.M.) Thomas Ferst, thomas.ferst@vtg.admin.ch

Weitere Informationen über die Dozentur Militärsoziologie an der Militärakademie (MILAK) an der ETH Zürich finden Sie auf unserer Webseite: https://www.vtg.admin.ch/de/dozentur-militarsoziologie . Für Auskünfte steht Ihnen lic. phil. MAS in Criminology (LL.M.) Thomas Ferst, stellvertretender Dozent Militärsoziologie und wissenschaftlicher Projektleiter der Studienreihe «Sicherheit», Tel. +41 58 484 82 73 oder E-Mail thomas.ferst@vtg.admin.ch , gerne zur Verfügung.

Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Training Network – Coupled Problems for Decarbonization in Industry and Power Generation (COMBINE)

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Training Network COMBINE brings together 17 academic institutions and 14 industrial partners across Europe.The network addresses key challenges in fluid structure interaction (FSI) relevant to energy, process, and materials engineering, with a strong focus on:

• Advanced numerical modelling and simulation

• Experimental methods and sensor technologies

• Data analysis of real-world monitoring data

• Artificial intelligence and machine learning for engineering applications

Researchers in COMBINE benefit from interdisciplinary, international,and inter-sectoral training, including secondments at leading academic and industrial partner institutions across Europe.

Project background

Project title: High resolution experimental measurements of vibrations in rods and rod bundles using ensemble average high-resolution gamma tomography measurements.

This project focuses on the development of advanced tomographic techniques to evalute vibrations in rod bundles. The research will leverage our in-house, state-of-the-art, high-resolution gamma tomography system.

Job description

• Construction of a setup with a single rod and a rod bundle

• Measurements of vibrating rod/rod-bundle using our in-house gamma-tomography system

• AI-assisted reconstruction and imaging of vibrating rods/bundles using sensors and tomography data

• Use of machine-learning for noise reduction and data enhancement

Profile

• Master's degree in engineering, physics, applied mathematics, computer science, or closely related field

• Strong background in mathematics and machine learning

• Programming proficiency in Python, C++ or similar

• Experience with data processing and model interpretation

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in an international research environment

• Good written and spoken English

• Hands-on experience with experimental setup and basic electronics understanding is of advantage

Workplace

We offer

• Excellent research environment

• Supervision by internationally recognized academic and industrial experts

• Network-wide training events and local courses in technical and transferable skills

• International secondments at academic and industrial partner institutions across Europe

• Competitive salary

• les méthodes expérimentales et les technologies de capteurs

Contexte du projet Titre du projet : Mesures expérimentales à haute résolution des vibrations dans les tiges et les faisceaux de tiges à l'aide de mesures tomographiques gamma moyennes à haute résolution de l'ensemble. jobs.description:
MaP Executive Director

80%-100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH Zürich Competence Center for Materials and Processes ( MaP ) is a multidisciplinary scientific network devoted to tackling the grand challenges in materials, processes and manufacturing technologies. We foster cross-disciplinary research, education, and outreach to other academic institutes, industry and society in this field. Current major initiatives of MaP are the MaP Doctoral School and ETH Sabbatical | CAS AMaP continuing education programme. To lead the executive office as the central coordination hub, MaP is currently hiring a new Executive Director, starting from 1 July 2026 or earlier on agreement.

Project background

We are seeking an individual who is highly motivated to manage and develop MaP , together with the Steering Committee and the community of over 80 affiliated research groups . The Executive Director is responsible for leading the executive office, including managing strategy, human resources, finances, as well as operations and activities, governance and communications. The main focus of this key interfacing role is on community building and managing multi-stakeholder collaboration across a broad range of themes, therefore requiring a broad understanding of the grand challenges in Materials and Processes. The position embraces the designing, managing and overseeing of all research, education and outreach programs of MaP , including the MaP Doctoral School and ETH Sabbatical | CAS AMaP .

Job description

Strategic Leadership & Office Management

• Manage and develop MaP in close collaboration with the Steering Committee and a community of over 80 affiliated research groups.

• Lead the executive office, taking full responsibility for its operations and daily activities.

• Oversee core management areas, including strategy, human resources, finances, and governance.

Collaboration & Community Building

• Foster community building and manage multi-stakeholder collaboration across a broad range of themes.

• Act as a key interface between various research groups and research entities.

• Direct/Develop communication strategies to engage and connect the MaP community.

Program Management & Oversight

• Design, manage, and oversee all MaP research, education, and outreach programs.

• Direct specific initiatives, including the MaP Doctoral School and the ETH Sabbatical | CAS AMaP.

Profile

• The successful candidate has a strong academic background in science and/or engineering and ample work experience in topics relevant to Materials and Processes.

• Given the requirement to work across disciplines, sectors and cultures, the candidate must have excellent communication and organisational skills and experience in community building and further participatory processes.

• Strong project and business management skills are essential, from strategy and conceptualisation to planning and effective implementation, along with budgeting, financial management, evaluation and reporting.

• The ability to work in a motivated, independent, responsible, resourceful and resilient manner is vital.

• And, ideally, the candidate has already gained some hands-on experience in managing people, having budget responsibility and running research projects and education programs. Fluency in English and German is required.

Workplace

We offer

We offer a dynamic work environment with a high degree of freedom in design and implementation and many opportunities for an individual with commensurate qualifications, a can-do attitude, and a proactive and creative mindset to further her/his professional goals. The position is limited to one year, with the possibility of extension depending on the further development of MaP and its initiatives.

descriptionByLocale.en:
MaP Executive Director

80%-100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH Zürich Competence Center for Materials and Processes ( MaP ) is a multidisciplinary scientific network devoted to tackling the grand challenges in materials, processes and manufacturing technologies. We foster cross-disciplinary research, education, and outreach to other academic institutes, industry and society in this field. Current major initiatives of MaP are the MaP Doctoral School and ETH Sabbatical | CAS AMaP continuing education programme. To lead the executive office as the central coordination hub, MaP is currently hiring a new Executive Director, starting from 1 July 2026 or earlier on agreement.

Project background

We are seeking an individual who is highly motivated to manage and develop MaP , together with the Steering Committee and the community of over 80 affiliated research groups . The Executive Director is responsible for leading the executive office, including managing strategy, human resources, finances, as well as operations and activities, governance and communications. The main focus of this key interfacing role is on community building and managing multi-stakeholder collaboration across a broad range of themes, therefore requiring a broad understanding of the grand challenges in Materials and Processes. The position embraces the designing, managing and overseeing of all research, education and outreach programs of MaP , including the MaP Doctoral School and ETH Sabbatical | CAS AMaP .

Job description

Strategic Leadership & Office Management

• Manage and develop MaP in close collaboration with the Steering Committee and a community of over 80 affiliated research groups.

• Lead the executive office, taking full responsibility for its operations and daily activities.

• Oversee core management areas, including strategy, human resources, finances, and governance.

Collaboration & Community Building

• Foster community building and manage multi-stakeholder collaboration across a broad range of themes.

• Act as a key interface between various research groups and research entities.

• Direct/Develop communication strategies to engage and connect the MaP community.

Program Management & Oversight

• Design, manage, and oversee all MaP research, education, and outreach programs.

• Direct specific initiatives, including the MaP Doctoral School and the ETH Sabbatical | CAS AMaP.

Profile

• The successful candidate has a strong academic background in science and/or engineering and ample work experience in topics relevant to Materials and Processes.

• Given the requirement to work across disciplines, sectors and cultures, the candidate must have excellent communication and organisational skills and experience in community building and further participatory processes.

• Strong project and business management skills are essential, from strategy and conceptualisation to planning and effective implementation, along with budgeting, financial management, evaluation and reporting.

• The ability to work in a motivated, independent, responsible, resourceful and resilient manner is vital.

• And, ideally, the candidate has already gained some hands-on experience in managing people, having budget responsibility and running research projects and education programs. Fluency in English and German is required.

Workplace

We offer

We offer a dynamic work environment with a high degree of freedom in design and implementation and many opportunities for an individual with commensurate qualifications, a can-do attitude, and a proactive and creative mindset to further her/his professional goals. The position is limited to one year, with the possibility of extension depending on the further development of MaP and its initiatives.

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity,

Leiter:in Alarmorganisation (m/w/d)

100%, Zürich, unbefristet

print
Drucken

Die Abteilung Facility Services stellt das technische und infrastrukturelle Gebäudemanagement aller von der ETH Zürich genutzten Gebäude und Räume sicher. Die angegliederte Alarmorganisation gliedert sich in die Teilbereiche Alarmzentrale (AZ) und Sicherheitsdienst (SiDi) und arbeitet im 3-Schichtbetrieb (24/7/365). Die Alarmzentrale ist die Anlaufstelle für sämtliche Vorkommnisse im Personen-, Gebäude- und Anlagenschutz. Der Sicherheitsdienst ist verantwortlich für die Kontrolle der sicherheitstechnischen Einrichtungen in den Gebäuden und die Erstintervention im Ereignisfall.

Bereit, Verantwortung zu übernehmen, wenn jede Sekunde zählt?

Sie kennen den Alltag in einer Alarmorganisation nicht nur – sie leben ihn. Sie bleiben ruhig, wenn andere hektisch werden, treffen Entscheidungen mit klarem Kopf und führen Ihr Team auch unter Druck sicher ans Ziel? Dann wartet hier Ihre nächste Herausforderung als Leiter:in Alarmorganisation (m/w/d).

Gestalten Sie die Alarmorganisation der ETH Zürich aktiv mit und sorgen dafür, dass Sicherheit jederzeit gewährleistet ist.

Stellenbeschreibung

Ihre Aufgaben – Verantwortung, Wirkung und Gestaltungsspielraum

In dieser Schlüsselposition übernehmen Sie die Gesamtverantwortung für die Alarmorganisation der ETH Zürich mit rund 20 Mitarbeitenden (inkl. 4 Direktunterstellten). Sie stellen sicher, dass sämtliche Ereignisse im Personen-, Gebäude- und Anlagenschutz an allen ETH-Standorten im 24/7/365-Betrieb professionell, effizient und zuverlässig bewältigt werden.

Sie führen die Teamleitung der Alarmzentrale, des Sicherheitsdienstes sowie die Fachstelle IT AMS und sorgen gemeinsam mit ihnen für eine hochverfügbare, qualitativ exzellente Leistungserbringung. Dabei haben Sie stets im Blick, dass Alarmzentrale und Sicherheitsdienst eine sichtbare Visitenkarte der ETH sind – entsprechend setzen Sie auf Professionalität, Respekt und einem starken Teamauftritt.

Ein zentraler Teil Ihrer Arbeit ist die Weiterentwicklung der Organisation: Sie analysieren bestehende Abläufe, optimieren Prozesse gezielt und treiben die Digitalisierung voran. Sie stellen sicher, dass Systeme wie AMS auf dem neuesten Stand sind und definieren technische Tools, die den operativen Alltag effizient unterstützen. Gleichzeitig garantieren Sie die konsequente Einhaltung aller gesetzlichen sowie ETH-internen Vorgaben.

Sie führen strukturierte Qualitätsprüfungen und Debriefings durch, leiten konkrete Verbesserungsmassnahmen ab und sorgen dafür, dass die Organisation kontinuierlich dazulernt und sich weiterentwickelt.

In Ihrer Führungsrolle setzen Sie klare Ziele, delegieren wirkungsvoll und schaffen Transparenz. Sie entwickeln Ihre Mitarbeitenden aktiv weiter – durch Standortbestimmungen, Schulungen, Talentförderung und vorausschauende Nachfolgeplanung. Auch in herausfordernden Situationen bleiben Sie präsent, treffen schnelle Entscheidungen und führen Ihr Team souverän durch herausfordernde Lagen.

Zusätzlich verantworten Sie zentrale organisatorische Aufgaben wie Budgetplanung, Schichtplanung sowie die Einhaltung von Finanz- und Beschaffungsrichtlinien. Sie koordinieren die Zusammenarbeit mit internen Schnittstellen, stellen den Informationsfluss zur Abteilungsleitung sicher und sorgen für eine klare, stufengerechte Kommunikation.

Darüber hinaus leiten Sie Projekte und arbeiten aktiv in bereichsübergreifenden Initiativen mit und gestalten so die Weiterentwicklung der Alarmorganisation nachhaltig mit. Durch kontinuierliche Aus- und Weiterbildung bleiben Sie fachlich und methodisch am Puls der Zeit.

Profil

• Abgeschlossene Berufslehre sowie Abschluss als Fachmann/-frau für Sicherheit und Bewachung, den Fachaus

Responsabile Organizzazione allarmi (m/f/d) 100%, Zurigo, stampa permanente Stampa Il dipartimento Facility Services garantisce la gestione tecnica e infrastrutturale di tutti gli edifici e locali utilizzati dall'ETH di Zurigo. L'organizzazione allarme convenzionata è suddivisa nelle sottoaree centrale allarme (AZ) e servizio sicurezza (SiDi) e opera su 3 turni (24 ore su 24, 7 giorni su 7, 365 giorni l'anno). La centrale allarmi è il punto di contatto per tutti gli incidenti relativi alla protezione delle persone, degli edifici e degli impianti. Il servizio di sicurezza è responsabile del controllo delle dotazioni di sicurezza degli edifici e del primo intervento in caso di incidente. Pronto ad assumerti la responsabilità quando ogni secondo conta? Non solo conoscono la vita quotidiana in un’organizzazione di allarme, ma la vivono. Rimani calmo quando gli altri sono frenetici, prendi decisioni con la mente lucida e guidi la tua squadra in sicurezza verso i propri obiettivi anche sotto pressione? Allora qui ti aspetta la tua prossima sfida come capo dell'organizzazione di allarme (m/f/d). Contribuite attivamente a definire l'organizzazione degli allarmi dell'ETH di Zurigo e assicuratevi che la sicurezza sia sempre garantita. Descrizione del lavoro I tuoi compiti: responsabilità, impatto e spazio per la creatività In questa posizione chiave assumerai la responsabilità generale dell'organizzazione degli allarmi presso l'ETH di Zurigo con circa 20 dipendenti (di cui 4 dipendenti diretti). Garantiscono che tutti gli eventi di protezione delle persone, degli edifici e delle strutture in tutte le sedi dell'ETH siano gestiti in modo professionale, efficiente e affidabile 24 ore su 24, 7 giorni su 7, 365 giorni all'anno. Dirigi la gestione del team della centrale di allarme, del servizio di sicurezza e del reparto IT AMS e, insieme a loro, garantisci una fornitura di servizi altamente disponibile e di eccellente qualità. Tieni sempre presente che la centrale d'allarme e il servizio di sicurezza sono un biglietto da visita visibile dell'ETH, quindi fai affidamento sulla professionalità, sul rispetto e su una forte presenza di squadra. Una parte centrale del tuo lavoro è l'ulteriore sviluppo dell'organizzazione: analizzi i processi esistenti, ottimizzi i processi in modo mirato e porti avanti la digitalizzazione. Garantisci che sistemi come AMS/AHF siano aggiornati e definisci strumenti tecnici che supportano in modo efficiente le operazioni quotidiane. Allo stesso tempo garantite il rispetto costante di tutti i requisiti legali e interni dell'ETH. Eseguite controlli di qualità e debriefing strutturati, ricavate misure di miglioramento concrete e assicurate che l'organizzazione impari e si sviluppi continuamente. Nel tuo ruolo di leadership, stabilisci obiettivi chiari, deleghi in modo efficace e crei trasparenza. Fai crescere attivamente i tuoi dipendenti – attraverso valutazioni delle sedi, formazione, sviluppo dei talenti e pianificazione della successione lungimirante. Anche in situazioni difficili, rimani presente, prendi decisioni rapide e guidi con sicurezza la tua squadra attraverso situazioni difficili. Inoltre, sarai responsabile di compiti organizzativi centrali come la pianificazione del budget, la pianificazione dei turni e il rispetto delle linee guida finanziarie e di approvvigionamento. Die Abteilung Facility Services stellt das technische und infrastrukturelle Gebäudemanagement aller von der ETH Zürich genutzten Gebäude und Räume sicher. Die angegliederte Alarmorganisation gliedert sich in die Teilbereiche Alarmzentrale (AZ) und Sicherheitsdienst (SiDi) und arbeitet im 3-Schichtbetrieb (24/7/365). Die Alarmzentrale ist die Anlaufstelle für sämtliche Vorkommnisse im Personen-, Gebäude- und Anlagenschutz. Der Sicherheitsdienst ist verantwortlich für die Kontrolle der sicherheitstechnischen Einrichtungen in den Gebäuden und die Erstintervention im Ereignisfall.

Bereit, Verantwortung zu übernehmen, wenn jede Sekunde zählt?

Sie kennen den Alltag in einer Alarmorganisation nicht nur – sie leben ihn. Sie bleiben ruhig, wenn andere hektisch werden, treffen Entscheidungen mit klarem Kopf und führen Ihr Team auch unter Druck sicher ans Ziel? Dann wartet hier Ihre nächste Herausforderung als Leiter:in Alarmorganisation (m/w/d).

Gestalten Sie die Alarmorganisation der ETH Zürich aktiv mit und sorgen dafür, dass Sicherheit jederzeit gewährleistet ist.

Stellenbeschreibung

Ihre Aufgaben – Verantwortung, Wirkung und Gestaltungsspielraum

In dieser Schlüsselposition übernehmen Sie die Gesamtverantwortung für die Alarmorganisation der ETH Zürich mit rund 20 Mitarbeitenden (inkl. 4 Direktunterstellten). Sie stellen sicher, dass sämtliche Ereignisse im Personen-, Gebäude- und Anlagenschutz an allen ETH-Standorten im 24/7/365-Betrieb professionell, effizient und zuverlässig bewältigt werden.

Sie führen die Teamleitung der Alarmzentrale, des Sicherheitsdienstes sowie die Fachstelle IT AMS und sorgen gemeinsam mit ihnen für eine hochverfügbare, qualitativ exzellente Leistungserbringung. Dabei haben Sie stets im Blick, dass Alarmzentrale und Sicherheitsdienst eine sichtbare Visitenkarte der ETH sind – entsprechend setzen Sie auf Professionalität, Respekt und einem starken Teamauftritt.

Ein zentraler Teil Ihrer Arbeit ist die Weiterentwicklung der Organisation: Sie analysieren bestehende Abläufe, optimieren Prozesse gezielt und treiben die Digitalisierung voran. Sie stellen sicher, dass Systeme wie AMS auf dem neuesten Stand sind und definieren technische Tools, die den operativen Alltag effizient unterstützen. Gleichzeitig garantieren Sie die konsequente Einhaltung aller gesetzlichen sowie ETH-internen Vorgaben.

Sie führen strukturierte Qualitätsprüfungen und Debriefings durch, leiten konkrete Verbesserungsmassnahmen ab und sorgen dafür, dass die Organisation kontinuierlich dazulernt und sich weiterentwickelt.

In Ihrer Führungsrolle setzen Sie klare Ziele, delegieren wirkungsvoll und schaffen Transparenz. Sie entwickeln Ihre Mitarbeitenden aktiv weiter – durch Standortbestimmungen, Schulungen, Talentförderung und vorausschauende Nachfolgeplanung. Auch in herausfordernden Situationen bleiben Sie präsent, treffen schnelle Entscheidungen und führen Ihr Team souverän durch herausfordernde Lagen.

Zusätzlich verantworten Sie zentrale organisatorische Aufgaben wie Budgetplanung, Schichtplanung sowie die Einhaltung von Finanz- und Beschaffungsrichtlinien. Sie koordinieren die Zusammenarbeit mit internen Schnittstellen, stellen den Informationsfluss zur Abteilungsleitung sicher und sorgen für eine klare, stufengerechte Kommunikation.

Darüber hinaus leiten Sie Projekte und arbeiten aktiv in bereichsübergreifenden Initiativen mit und gestalten so die Weiterentwicklung der Alarmorganisation nachhaltig mit. Durch kontinuierliche Aus- und Weiterbildung bleiben Sie fachlich und methodisch am Puls der Zeit.

Profil

jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Researcher in Light-Driven CO2 Capture

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Electrochemical Energy Systems Laboratory in the Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering at ETH Zurich invites applications for a Postdoctoral Researcher position focused on light-driven CO2 capture.

Job description

• Our group is actively developing a novel photoacid-based approach for efficient CO2 capture, optimizing both the local chemical environment in photoacids and their molecular structure to enhance sorption capacity and stability

• We seek a postdoctoral researcher who will contribute to these efforts

• You will join a diverse, inclusive, and supportive work environment that values scientific curiosity and creativity

Profile

• PhD in Physical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Material Science, or a related field

• Experience with in situ spectroscopy is a plus

• Excellent written and spoken English

• Self-driven, highly motivated, and strong teamwork skills

We welcome applications from candidates with expertise in organic synthesis and one or more of the following areas:

• Photochemistry

• Advanced characterization techniques (e.g., synchrotron facilities, in-situ methods)

• CO2 capture / utilization is a plus

We are looking for highly motivated researchers with a passion for contributing to solutions in the global energy landscape. If you excel in collaborative environments and can bring expertise in some of the areas listed above, we encourage you to apply.

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application please submit the following documents as a single merged PDF named with your last name, initials, and application date (e.g., 20250206_SmithJT_application) in the following order:

• Cover Letter describing your research achievements and interests

• Detailed CV

• Three Representative Published Works

• Names and Contact Information of at Least Three References

• Official Transcripts of All Degrees or a PhD degree confirmation, if available (in English)

In the field for additional information, please include your PhD, MSc, and BSc degree details (university, dates, and relevant experience).

Further information about our group can be found on our Website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Melanie Darugna, mdarugna@ethz.ch (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

This is a full-time position, tentatively starting on 15 July 2026, or later. Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.

jobs.description:
PhD position in Global Trade, Supply Chains and Climate Shocks

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

Research Division KOF Lab of ETH Zurich’s KOF Swiss Economic Institute is seeking a PhD candidate to study the propagation of weather and climate shocks in quantitative trade network models. The position is part of the National Centre of Competence in Research project Climate Extremes and Society: Strengthening Resilience (NCCR CLIM+). NCCR CLIM+ is a new, interdisciplinary, Switzerland-wide climate research community involving multiple investigators at ETH Zurich and other Swiss institutions.

Job description

• The project at KOF Lab will center around assessing and promoting the resilience of supply chains by building and solving quantitative global equilibrium models of trade networks.

• We will use firm-level data to estimate the industry/country-level effects of various weather and climate shocks and input the estimated impacts into the model.

• To this end, the doctoral candidate will leverage theoretical, computational, and econometric tools to study public policy questions related to the resilience of global supply chains to climate change.

• The doctorate will be conducted within the doctoral program of D-MTEC (Department of Management, Technology, and Economics) and is expected to be completed within four years.

• The candidate will be supervised primarily by Professor Hans Gersbach and Dr. Kieran Walsh.

• The position is for up to four years. The salary is in accordance with the PhD regulations of the Swiss National Science Foundation, which funds the NCCR.

Profile

• The applicant should have a master’s degree in economics or finance. We will also consider candidates with a master’s degree in mathematics or statistics, provided they have completed some coursework in economics and are prepared to do intensive economics PhD training.

• Applicants must be highly proficient in English.

• The applicant should be proficient in either MATLAB, Python, or Julia and willing to work in MATLAB.

• Prior coursework in (i) trade theory and (ii) environmental economics would be a major asset.

• Experience with panel data econometrics would be beneficial.

Workplace

We offer

• We offer the opportunity to apply cutting-edge economic theory to practical policy issues at the intersection of trade and climate change.

• Candidates will have the opportunity to contribute to NCCR CLIM+ research discussions.

• We offer the opportunity to join KOF, which is Switzerland’s leading academic institute for applied economic research. It provides independent and objective data and facts, as well as timely assessments to support decision-makers in politics and business in making fact-based decisions for the benefit of Swiss society.

• KOF PhD students are part of a large and vibrant community of economic researchers. The broader economics community in Zurich offers the opportunity to participate in numerous workshops and conferences spanning all fields of economics.

jobs.description:
PhD Position in AI-Supported Resilience Assessment of Climate-Neutral Transport Infrastructure

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Infrastructure Management, led by Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey within the Institute of Construction and Infrastructure Management of the Department of Civil, Environmental, and Geomatic Engineering, has an opening for a PhD student in transport infrastructure resilience. The position is part of the EU Horizon project SHIFTIN, which aims to accelerate the transition towards climate-neutral, resilient, and biodiversity-friendly transport infrastructure by 2050.

The doctoral research will focus on developing AI-supported stress-testing and surrogate-modelling methodologies to assess the resilience of interdependent transport infrastructure systems under climate-related and multi-hazard scenarios. The work will support rapid, evidence-based evaluation of design, retrofit, maintenance, and recovery strategies at asset, corridor, and network scales.

Project background

SHIFTIN is an EU Horizon project that aims to accelerate the transition towards climate-neutral, resilient, and biodiversity-friendly transport infrastructure by 2050. Roads, railways, and ports are essential for European mobility and economic activity, but they also consume large volumes of raw materials, generate greenhouse-gas and air-pollutant emissions, fragment habitats, and are increasingly exposed to climate-related hazards such as floods, landslides, and heatwaves.

To address these challenges, SHIFTIN will demonstrate and combine circular low-carbon construction materials, nature-based solutions, advanced monitoring technologies, and digital decision-support tools. Full-scale pilots on four TEN-T corridors will cover road, rail, and port contexts, integrating infrastructure monitoring, satellite and on-board sensing, IoT-enabled structural health monitoring, and AI-supported analytics.

A Digital Twin-based Integrated Decision Support Platform will convert monitoring and modelling outputs into transparent whole-life indicators for carbon, circularity, resilience, biodiversity, and costs. These outputs will support robust business cases, maintenance planning, green public procurement, and the wider uptake of sustainable and resilient infrastructure solutions across European transport networks.

Within this broader project, the PhD research will focus on AI-supported stress-testing and surrogate modelling for transport infrastructure resilience. The goal is to enable rapid assessment of many hazard, disruption, recovery, and intervention scenarios, supporting practical decision-making for climate-resilient and sustainable transport systems.

Job description

This doctorate aims to advance the state of the art in simulation-informed, AI-supported resilience assessment for transport infrastructure. Working closely with academic, industry, infrastructure, and public-sector partners across Europe, the candidate will contribute to the development of stress-testing frameworks, surrogate modelling algorithms, and decision-support tools for climate-resilient and sustainable transport systems. The candidate’s core tasks will include:

• Developing AI-supported surrogate models for infrastructure stress testing

• Linking surrogate models with agent-based and network-based simulations

• Assessing infrastructure interdependencies and recovery constraints

• Supporting resilience assessment across asset, corridor, and network scales

• Contributing to cost-benefit and decision-support analysis

• Addressing uncertainty, reliability, and explainability

• Integrating results with digital-twin and monitoring data

• Collaborating with the European project consortium

Profile

• A Master’s degree in civil engineering, transport engineering, infrastructure systems, environmental engineering, computational engineering, data science, or a closely related field

• Strong quantitative and programming skills, preferably

Posizione di dottorato in valutazione della resilienza supportata dall'intelligenza artificiale di infrastrutture di trasporto a impatto climatico zero 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Drucken La cattedra di gestione delle infrastrutture, guidata dal professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey all'interno dell'Istituto di costruzione e gestione delle infrastrutture del Dipartimento di ingegneria civile, ambientale e geomatica, ha un posto vacante per uno studente di dottorato in resilienza delle infrastrutture di trasporto. La posizione fa parte del progetto EU Horizon SHIFTIN, che mira ad accelerare la transizione verso infrastrutture di trasporto climaticamente neutre, resilienti e rispettose della biodiversità entro il 2050. La ricerca di dottorato si concentrerà sullo sviluppo di stress test supportati dall'intelligenza artificiale e di metodologie di modellazione surrogata per valutare la resilienza dei sistemi infrastrutturali di trasporto interdipendenti in scenari legati al clima e multi-rischio. Il lavoro supporterà una valutazione rapida e basata sull’evidenza delle strategie di progettazione, ammodernamento, manutenzione e ripristino a livello di asset, corridoio e rete. Contesto del progetto SHIFTIN è un progetto Horizon dell’UE che mira ad accelerare la transizione verso infrastrutture di trasporto climaticamente neutre, resilienti e rispettose della biodiversità entro il 2050. Strade, ferrovie e porti sono essenziali per la mobilità e l’attività economica europea, ma consumano anche grandi volumi di materie prime, generano emissioni di gas serra e inquinanti atmosferici, frammentano gli habitat e sono sempre più esposti a rischi legati al clima come inondazioni, frane e ondate di caldo. Per affrontare queste sfide, SHIFTIN dimostrerà e combinerà materiali da costruzione circolari a basse emissioni di carbonio, soluzioni basate sulla natura, tecnologie di monitoraggio avanzate e strumenti digitali di supporto alle decisioni. I progetti pilota su vasta scala su quattro corridoi TEN-T copriranno contesti stradali, ferroviari e portuali, integrando il monitoraggio delle infrastrutture, il rilevamento satellitare e di bordo, il monitoraggio della salute strutturale abilitato dall’IoT e l’analisi supportata dall’intelligenza artificiale. Una piattaforma integrata di supporto alle decisioni basata sul digital twin convertirà i risultati del monitoraggio e della modellazione in indicatori trasparenti per l’intero ciclo vitale di carbonio, circolarità, resilienza, biodiversità e costi. Questi risultati supporteranno solidi casi aziendali, pianificazione della manutenzione, appalti pubblici verdi e una più ampia adozione di soluzioni infrastrutturali sostenibili e resilienti nelle reti di trasporto europee. L’obiettivo è consentire una rapida valutazione di molti scenari di pericolo, interruzione, ripresa e intervento, supportando il processo decisionale pratico per sistemi di trasporto resilienti al clima e sostenibili. Lavorando a stretto contatto con partner accademici, industriali, infrastrutturali e del settore pubblico in tutta Europa, il candidato contribuirà allo sviluppo di quadri di stress test, algoritmi di modellazione surrogati e strumenti di supporto decisionale per sistemi di trasporto resilienti al clima e sostenibili. • Sviluppare modelli surrogati supportati dall'intelligenza artificiale per stress test delle infrastrutture

• Supportare la valutazione della resilienza su scale di risorse, corridoi e reti

PhD Position in AI-Supported Resilience Assessment of Climate-Neutral Transport Infrastructure

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Infrastructure Management, led by Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey within the Institute of Construction and Infrastructure Management of the Department of Civil, Environmental, and Geomatic Engineering, has an opening for a PhD student in transport infrastructure resilience. The position is part of the EU Horizon project SHIFTIN, which aims to accelerate the transition towards climate-neutral, resilient, and biodiversity-friendly transport infrastructure by 2050.

The doctoral research will focus on developing AI-supported stress-testing and surrogate-modelling methodologies to assess the resilience of interdependent transport infrastructure systems under climate-related and multi-hazard scenarios. The work will support rapid, evidence-based evaluation of design, retrofit, maintenance, and recovery strategies at asset, corridor, and network scales.

Project background

SHIFTIN is an EU Horizon project that aims to accelerate the transition towards climate-neutral, resilient, and biodiversity-friendly transport infrastructure by 2050. Roads, railways, and ports are essential for European mobility and economic activity, but they also consume large volumes of raw materials, generate greenhouse-gas and air-pollutant emissions, fragment habitats, and are increasingly exposed to climate-related hazards such as floods, landslides, and heatwaves.

To address these challenges, SHIFTIN will demonstrate and combine circular low-carbon construction materials, nature-based solutions, advanced monitoring technologies, and digital decision-support tools. Full-scale pilots on four TEN-T corridors will cover road, rail, and port contexts, integrating infrastructure monitoring, satellite and on-board sensing, IoT-enabled structural health monitoring, and AI-supported analytics.

A Digital Twin-based Integrated Decision Support Platform will convert monitoring and modelling outputs into transparent whole-life indicators for carbon, circularity, resilience, biodiversity, and costs. These outputs will support robust business cases, maintenance planning, green public procurement, and the wider uptake of sustainable and resilient infrastructure solutions across European transport networks.

Within this broader project, the PhD research will focus on AI-supported stress-testing and surrogate modelling for transport infrastructure resilience. The goal is to enable rapid assessment of many hazard, disruption, recovery, and intervention scenarios, supporting practical decision-making for climate-resilient and sustainable transport systems.

Job description

This doctorate aims to advance the state of the art in simulation-informed, AI-supported resilience assessment for transport infrastructure. Working closely with academic, industry, infrastructure, and public-sector partners across Europe, the candidate will contribute to the development of stress-testing frameworks, surrogate modelling algorithms, and decision-support tools for climate-resilient and sustainable transport systems. The candidate’s core tasks will include:

• Developing AI-supported surrogate models for infrastructure stress testing

• Linking surrogate models with agent-based and network-based simulations

• Assessing infrastructure interdependencies and recovery constraints

• Supporting resilience assessment across asset, corridor, and network scales

• Contributing to cost-benefit and decision-support analysis

• Addressing uncertainty, reliability, and explainability

• Integrating results with digital-twin and monitoring data

• Collaborating with the European project consortium

Profile

• A Master’s degree in civil engineering, transport engineering, infrastructure systems, environmental engineering, computational engineering, data science, or a closely related field

• Strong quantitative and programming skills, preferably

Poste de doctorat en évaluation de la résilience des infrastructures de transport climatiquement neutres par l'IA à 100 %, Zurich, impression à durée déterminée Drucken La chaire de gestion des infrastructures, dirigée par le professeur Dr Bryan T. Adey au sein de l'Institut de construction et de gestion des infrastructures du Département de génie civil, environnemental et géomatique, a une ouverture pour un doctorant en résilience des infrastructures de transport. Le poste fait partie du projet Horizon de l'UE SHIFTIN, qui vise à accélérer la transition vers des infrastructures de transport neutres pour le climat, résilientes et respectueuses de la biodiversité d'ici 2050. La recherche doctorale se concentrera sur le développement de méthodologies de tests de résistance et de modélisation de substitution basées sur l'IA pour évaluer la résilience des systèmes d'infrastructures de transport interdépendants dans des scénarios liés au climat et à plusieurs risques. Les travaux soutiendront une évaluation rapide et fondée sur des données probantes des stratégies de conception, de modernisation, de maintenance et de récupération à l’échelle des actifs, des corridors et du réseau. Contexte du projet SHIFTIN est un projet Horizon de l'UE qui vise à accélérer la transition vers des infrastructures de transport neutres pour le climat, résilientes et respectueuses de la biodiversité d'ici 2050. Les routes, les chemins de fer et les ports sont essentiels à la mobilité et à l'activité économique européennes, mais ils consomment également de grandes quantités de matières premières, génèrent des émissions de gaz à effet de serre et de polluants atmosphériques, fragmentent les habitats et sont de plus en plus exposés aux risques liés au climat tels que les inondations, les glissements de terrain et les vagues de chaleur. Pour relever ces défis, SHIFTIN démontrera et combinera des matériaux de construction circulaires à faible émission de carbone, des solutions basées sur la nature, des technologies de surveillance avancées et des outils numériques d'aide à la décision. Des projets pilotes à grande échelle sur quatre corridors RTE-T couvriront les contextes routiers, ferroviaires et portuaires, intégrant la surveillance des infrastructures, la détection par satellite et embarquée, la surveillance de l'état des structures grâce à l'IoT et les analyses basées sur l'IA. Une plateforme intégrée d'aide à la décision basée sur un jumeau numérique convertira les résultats de la surveillance et de la modélisation en indicateurs transparents sur toute la durée de vie du carbone, de la circularité, de la résilience, de la biodiversité et des coûts. Ces résultats soutiendront des analyses de rentabilisation solides, la planification de la maintenance, les marchés publics écologiques et l'adoption plus large de solutions d'infrastructure durables et résilientes dans les réseaux de transport européens. Dans le cadre de ce projet plus large, la recherche doctorale se concentrera sur les tests de résistance et la modélisation de substitution basés sur l'IA pour la résilience des infrastructures de transport. L’objectif est de permettre une évaluation rapide de nombreux scénarios de danger, de perturbation, de rétablissement et d’intervention, aidant ainsi la prise de décision pratique pour des systèmes de transport durables et résilients au climat. Description du poste Ce doctorat vise à faire progresser l'état de l'art en matière d'évaluation de la résilience des infrastructures de transport, basée sur la simulation et appuyée par l'IA. Travaillant en étroite collaboration avec des partenaires universitaires, industriels, infrastructurels et du secteur public à travers l'Europe, le candidat contribuera au développement de cadres de tests de résistance, d'algorithmes de modélisation de substitution et d'outils d'aide à la décision pour des systèmes de transport durables et résilients au climat. Les tâches principales du candidat comprendront :

• Lier les modèles de substitution avec des simulations basées sur des agents et des réseaux

• Soutenir l'évaluation de la résilience à l'échelle des actifs, des corridors et du réseau

• Gérer l'incertitude, la fiabilité et l'explicabilité

jobs.description:
PhD position in Computational earthquake rupture mechanics

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

At the Professorship of Solid Mechanics (SMEC) in the Institute for Building Materials at ETH Zurich, we aim to understand how materials deform, degrade, break, and ultimately fail. Our research is driven by curiosity about the physical mechanisms that underlie failure and by the ambition to translate this understanding into more reliable and resilient materials and structures. By combining numerical modeling, laboratory experiments, and theoretical analyses, we seek to link microscopic processes with the macroscopic behavior of both engineering and natural systems and develop predictive tools for mechanical failure.

Our team is highly interdisciplinary and international, bringing together researchers with backgrounds in materials science, mechanics, and applied physics. We work across a broad range of topics, including the mechanics of particle systems (colloidal and granular), architected and topologically interlocked materials, the mechanics of fragility in collagen, the mechanics of earthquakes, fracture of soft materials, and modeling failure in multiphysical processes such as corrosion-driven degradation of concrete. What unites these efforts is a shared curiosity about why complex materials fail and a commitment to developing new concepts, experiments, and models that advance our understanding of failure mechanics.

We are seeking a motivated, innovative PhD student with a background in computational mechanics to work on a project in computational earthquake rupture mechanics. The project will combine numerical method development and theoretical analysis to investigate how heterogeneous stress states and nonlinear near-fault processes influence earthquake rupture propagation, arrest, and earthquake-size statistics.

Job description

• You will conduct a computational and theoretical investigation of dynamic earthquake rupture, with a focus on rupture propagation, rupture arrest, and energy dissipation in heterogeneous fault systems

• The work will connect fracture-mechanics theory with large-scale numerical simulations of earthquake rupture

• You will develop, improve, and use high-performance simulation tools for dynamic rupture, including GPU-oriented numerical methods

• You will verify and validate the numerical methods against benchmark problems and established theoretical results

• Building on these tools, you will investigate how heterogeneous stress states and nonlinear dissipative processes, such as off-fault plasticity, influence rupture arrest and earthquake-size statistics

• The position provides a stimulating environment for scientific growth and collaboration

Profile

• You hold an MSc degree in mechanics, physics, engineering, earth science, material science, computational science, or a related discipline

• You have a background in computational mechanics, solid mechanics, applied physics, scientific computing, or a related field

• You have experience implementing scientific code and validating it against analytical solutions, numerical benchmarks, or well-documented reference results.

• You have prior programming experience in Python and have used version control. Experience with high-performance computing, GPU programming, C/C++, or numerical methods for wave propagation, fracture, or solid mechanics is an advantage

• You are curious, self-motivated, and enjoy developing numerical methods to answer mechanics questions

• You are fluent in English, both oral and written

• You enjoy working in a team, possess the necessary social skills and communication abilities, and contribute proactively to a positive group atmosphere

Workplace

We offer

• You will join a dynamic, international, and supportive research group that values curiosity, rigor, and collaboration.

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively

descriptionByLocale.it:
Descrizione Alla cattedra di Meccanica dei Solidi (SMEC) presso l'Istituto dei Materiali da Costruzione dell'ETH di Zurigo, miriamo a capire come i materiali si deformano, si degradano, si rompono e, infine, si guastano. La nostra ricerca è guidata dalla curiosità verso i meccanismi fisici che sono alla base dei cedimenti e dall’ambizione di tradurre questa comprensione in materiali e strutture più affidabili e resilienti. Combinando modellazione numerica, esperimenti di laboratorio e analisi teoriche, cerchiamo di collegare i processi microscopici con il comportamento macroscopico sia dei sistemi ingegneristici che naturali e di sviluppare strumenti predittivi per i guasti meccanici. Il nostro team è altamente interdisciplinare e internazionale e riunisce ricercatori con background in scienza dei materiali, meccanica e fisica applicata. Lavoriamo su un'ampia gamma di argomenti, tra cui la meccanica dei sistemi di particelle (colloidali e granulari), materiali strutturati e topologicamente interconnessi, la meccanica della fragilità del collagene, la meccanica dei terremoti, la frattura di materiali morbidi e la modellazione dei guasti in processi multifisici come il degrado del calcestruzzo causato dalla corrosione. Ciò che unisce questi sforzi è una curiosità condivisa sul perché i materiali complessi falliscono e l’impegno nello sviluppo di nuovi concetti, esperimenti e modelli che migliorino la nostra comprensione dei meccanismi dei guasti.
• Cerchiamo uno studente di dottorato motivato e innovativo con un background in meccanica computazionale per lavorare su un progetto sulla meccanica computazionale della rottura dei terremoti. Il progetto combinerà lo sviluppo di metodi numerici e l’analisi teorica per studiare come gli stati di stress eterogenei e i processi non lineari di quasi faglia influenzano la propagazione della rottura del terremoto, l’arresto e le statistiche sulle dimensioni del terremoto. Descrizione del lavoro - Condurre un'indagine computazionale e teorica sulla rottura dinamica del terremoto, con particolare attenzione alla propagazione della rottura, all'arresto della rottura e alla dissipazione di energia in sistemi di faglie eterogenei - Collegare la teoria della meccanica della frattura con simulazioni numeriche su larga scala della rottura del terremoto - Sviluppare, migliorare e utilizzare strumenti di simulazione ad alte prestazioni per la rottura dinamica, inclusi metodi numerici orientati alla GPU - Verificare e convalidare i metodi numerici rispetto a problemi di riferimento e risultati teorici consolidati - Investigare come gli stati di stress eterogenei e processi dissipativi non lineari, come plasticità fuori faglia, arresto di rottura e statistiche sulle dimensioni dei terremoti - Fornire un ambiente stimolante per la crescita scientifica e la collaborazione Profilo - Possedere un master in meccanica, fisica, ingegneria, scienze della terra, scienza dei materiali, scienze computazionali o una disciplina correlata - Avere esperienza in meccanica computazionale, meccanica dei solidi, fisica applicata, informatica scientifica o un campo correlato - Avere esperienza nell'implementazione di codice scientifico e nella sua convalida rispetto a soluzioni analitiche, benchmark numerici o risultati di riferimento ben documentati - Avere esperienza di programmazione precedente in Python e hanno utilizzato il controllo della versione. L'esperienza con il calcolo ad alte prestazioni, la programmazione GPU, C/C++ o metodi numerici per la propagazione delle onde, la frattura o la meccanica dei solidi costituisce un vantaggio - Essere curioso, automotivato e divertirsi nello sviluppo di metodi numerici per rispondere a domande di meccanica - Essere fluente in inglese, sia orale che scritto - Piacere lavorare in gruppo, possedere le necessarie abilità sociali e comunicative e contribuire in modo proattivo a un'atmosfera di gruppo positiva Cosa offerta - Partecipa a un gruppo di ricerca dinamico, internazionale e solidale che valorizza la curiosità, il rigore e la collaborazione - Il tuo lavoro ha un impatto: diventa parte dell'ETH di Zurigo, che non solo sostiene il tuo sviluppo professionale, ma contribuisce anche attivamente alla tua crescita professionale e al tuo successo
